1.1: Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt (every man and his housholde came thither with Iaakob)
1.4: Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
1.5: So al the soules, that came out of the loines of Iaakob, were seuentie soules: Joseph was in Egypt already.
1.6: Now Joseph died and all his brethren, and that whole generation.
1.7: And the children of Israel brought foorth fruit and encreased in aboundance, and were multiplied, and were exceeding mightie, so that the land was full of them.
1.8: Then there rose up a new King in Egypt, who knew not Joseph.
1.9: And he sayde unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are greater and mightier then we.
1.10: Come, let us work wisely with them, least they multiplie, and it come to pass, that if there be war, they ioyne them selves also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and get them out of the land.
1.11: Therefore did they set taskemasters over them, to keep the under with burdens: and they built the cities Pithom and Raamses for the treasures of Pharaoh.
1.12: But the more they vexed them, the more they multiplied and grew: therefore they were more grieved against the children of Israel.
1.13: Wherefore the Egyptians by crueltie caused the children of Israel to serve.
1.14: Thus they made them weary of their lives by sore labour in clay and in brick, and in al work in the field, with all maner of bondage, which they layde upon them most cruelly.
1.15: Moreover the King of Egypt commanded ye midwives of the Ebrewe women, (of which the ones name was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah)
1.16: And sayde, When ye doe the office of a midwife to the women of the Ebrewes, and see them on their stooles, if it be a sonne, then yee shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then let her live.
1.17: Notwithstanding ye midwives feared God, and did not as the King of Egypt commanded them, but preserved alive the men children.
1.18: Then the King of Egypt called for the midwives, and sayde unto them, Why have yee done thus, and have preserved alive the men children?
1.19: And the midwives answered Pharaoh, Because the Ebrewe women are not as the women of Egypt: for they are lively, and are delivered yer the midwife come at them.
1.20: God therefore prospered the midwives, and the people multiplied and were very mightie.
1.21: And because ye midwives feared God, therefore he made them houses.
1.22: Then Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every man child that is borne, cast yee into the river, but reserve every maid child alive.

2.1: Then there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi,
2.2: And the woman coceiued and bare a sonne: and when she saw that he was fair, she hid him three moneths.
2.3: But when she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark made of reed, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and laid the child therein, and put it among the bulrushes by the rivers brink.
2.4: Now his sister stood a far off, to wit what would come of him.
2.5: Then ye daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash her in the river, and her maidens walked by the rivers side: and when she saw the ark among the bulrushes, she sent her maid to fet it.
2.6: Then she opened it, and saw it was a child: and behold, the babe wept: so she had compassion on it, and sayde, This is one of the Ebrewes children.
2.7: Then said his sister unto Pharaohs daughter, Shall I go and cal unto thee a nurce of the Ebrew women to nurce thee the child?
2.8: And Pharaohs daughter sayde to her, Goe. So the maid went and called the childes mother,
2.9: To whom Pharaohs daughter sayde, Take this child away, and nurce it for me, and I wil reward thee. Then the woman took the child and nurced him.
2.10: Now the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaohs daughter, and he was as her sonne, and she called his name Moses, because, said she, I drew him out of the water.
2.11: And in those dayes, when Moses was growen, he went forth unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: also he saw an Egyptian smiting an Ebrewe one of his brethren.
2.12: And he looked round about, and when he saw no man, hee slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
2.13: Again he came forth the second day, and behold, two Ebrewes strove: and he said unto him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
2.14: And hee answered, Who made thee a man of authoritie, and a judge over us? Thinkest thou to kill mee, as thou killedst the Egyptian? Then Moses feared and sayde, Certainly this thing is knowen.
2.15: Now Pharaoh heard this matter, and sought to slay Moses: therefore Moses fled from Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian, and hee sat down by a well.
2.16: And the Priest of Midian had seue daughters, which came and drew water, and filled the troghes, for to water their fathers sheep.
2.17: Then the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses rose up and defended them, and watered their sheep.
2.18: And whe they came to Reuel their father, he said, How are ye come so soon to day?
2.19: And they said, A man of Egypt delivered us from the hand of the shepherdes, and also drew us water ynough, and watered the sheep.
2.20: Then he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why have ye so left the man? call him that he may eat bread.
2.21: And Moses agreed to dwell with the man: who gave unto Moses Zipporah his daughter:
2.22: And she bare a sonne, whose name he called Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.
2.23: Then in process of time, the King of Egypt dyed, and the children of Israel sighed for the bondage and cryed: and their crie for the bondage came up unto God.
2.24: Then God heard their mone, and God remembred his covenant with Abraham, Izhak, and Iaakob.
2.25: So God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.

3.1: When Moses kept the sheep of Jethro his father in law, Priest of Midian, and drove the flock to the back side of the desert, and came to the Mountain of God, Horeb,
3.2: Then the Angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a flame of fire, out of the middes of a bush: and he looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
3.3: Therefore Moses said, I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush burneth not.
3.4: And when the Lord saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the middes of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he answered, I am here.
3.5: Then he said, Come not hither, put thy shooes off thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
3.6: Moreover he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Izhak, and the God of Iaakob. Then Moses hid his face: for he was afraid to look upon God.
3.7: Then the Lord said, I have surely seen the trouble of my people, which are in Egypt, and have heard their crie, because of their taskemasters: for I know their sorowes.
3.8: Therefore I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them out of that land into a good land and a large, into a land that floweth with milk and honie, even into the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
3.9: And now lo, the crie of the children of Israel is come unto me, and I have also seen ye oppression, wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.
3.10: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou maiest bring my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
3.11: But Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?
3.12: And he answered, Certainely I will be with thee: and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee, After that thou hast brought the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this Mountain.
3.13: Then Moses said unto God, Behold, when I shall come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you: if they say unto me, What is his Name? what shall I say unto them?
3.14: And God answered Moses, I Am That I Am. Also he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I Am hath sent me unto you.
3.15: And God spake further unto Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Izhak, and the God of Iaakob hath sent me unto you: this is my Name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all ages.
3.16: Go and gather the Elders of Israel together, and thou shalt say unto the, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Izhak, and Iaakob appeared unto me, and said, I have surely remembred you, and that which is done to you in Egypt.
3.17: Therefore I did say, I wil bring you out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, unto a land that floweth with milk and honie.
3.18: Then shall they obey thy voyce, and thou and the Elders of Israel shall go unto the King of Egypt, and say unto him, The Lord God of the Ebrewes hath met with us: we pray thee now therefore, let us goe three dayes journey in the wilderness, that we may sacrifice unto the Lord our God.
3.19: But I know, that the King of Egypt wil not let you goe, but by strong hand.
3.20: Therefore will I stretch out mine hand and smite Egypt with all my wonders, which I will doe in the middes thereof: and after that shall he let you goe.
3.21: And I will make this people to be fauoured of the Egyptians: so that when ye go, ye shall not goe emptie.
3.22: For every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her that soiourneth in her house, jewels of silver and jewels of gold and raiment, and ye shall put them on your sonnes, and on your daughters, and shall spoyle the Egyptians.

4.1: Then Moses answered, and said, But lo, they will not beleeue me, nor hearken unto my voyce: for they will say, The Lord hath not appeared unto thee.
4.2: And the Lord said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he answered, A rod.
4.3: Then said he, Cast it on the ground. So he cast it on the ground, and it was turned into a serpent: and Moses fled from it.
4.4: Again the Lord said unto Moses, Put foorth thine hand, and take it by the tayle. Then he put foorth his hand and caught it, and it was turned into a rod in his hand.
4.5: Do this that they may beleeue, that the Lord God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Izhak, and the God of Iaakob hath appeared unto thee.
4.6: And the Lord said furthermore unto him, Thrust now thine hand into thy bosom. And he thrust his hand into his bosom, and when he took it out again, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.
4.7: Moreover he said, Put thine hand into thy bosom again. So he put his hand into his bosom again, and pluckt it out of his bosom, and behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.
4.8: So shall it be, if they wil not beleeue thee, neither obey the voyce of ye first sign, yet shall they beleeue for the voyce of the second sign.
4.9: But if they will not yet beleeue these two signes, neither obey unto thy voyce, then shalt thou take of the water of the river, and powre it upon the drie land: so the water which thou shalt take out of the river, shalbe turned to blood upon the drie land.
4.10: But Moses said unto the Lord, Oh my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither at any time have been, nor yet since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speach and slow of tongue.
4.11: Then the Lord said unto him, Who hath given the mouth to man? or who hath made the domme, or the deaf, or him that seeth, or the blind? have not I the Lord?
4.12: Therefore goe now, and I will be with thy mouth, and will teach thee what thou shalt say.
4.13: But he said, Oh my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him, whom thou shouldest send.
4.14: Then the Lord was verie angrie with Moses, and said, Doe not I know Aaron thy brother the Levite, that he himself shall speak? for loe, he cometh also foorth to meet thee, and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
4.15: Therefore thou shalt speak unto him, and put the wordes in his mouth, and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye ought to doe.
4.16: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be as thy mouth, and thou shalt be to him as God.
4.17: Moreover thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do miracles.
4.18: Therefore Moses went and returned to Jethro his father in law, and said unto him, I pray thee, let me goe, and return to my brethren, which are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. Then Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
4.19: (For the Lord had said unto Moses in Midian, Goe, return to Egypt: for they are all dead which went about to kill thee)
4.20: Then Moses took his wife, and his sonnes, and put them on an ass, and returned toward the land of Egypt, and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.
4.21: And the Lord said unto Moses, When thou art entred and come into Egypt again, see that thou doe all the wonders before Pharaoh, which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, and he shall not let the people goe.
4.22: Then thou shalt say to Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my sonne, even my first borne.
4.23: Wherefore I say to thee, Let my sonne go, that he may serve me: if thou refuse to let him goe, behold, I will slay thy sonne, even thy first borne.
4.24: And as he was by the way in the ynne, the Lord met him, and would have killed him.
4.25: Then Zipporah took a sharp knife, and cut away the foreskinne of her sonne, and cast it at his feet, and said, Thou art indeed a bloody husband unto me.
4.26: So he departed from him. Then she said, O bloodie husband (because of the circumcision)
4.27: Then the Lord said unto Aaron, Goe meet Moses in the wilderness. And he went and met him in the Mount of God, and kissed him.
4.28: Then Moses told Aaron all the wordes of the Lord, who had sent him, and all the signes wherewith he had charged him.
4.29: So went Moses and Aaron, and gathered all the Elders of the children of Israel.
4.30: And Aaron told all the wordes, which the Lord had spoken unto Moses, and he did the miracles in the sight of the people,
4.31: And the people beleeued, and when they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and had looked upon their tribulation, they bowed down, and worshipped.

5.1: Then afterward Moses and Aaron went and said to Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may celebrate a feast unto me in the wilderness.
5.2: And Pharaoh said, Who is the Lord, that I should hear his voyce, and let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel goe.
5.3: And they said, We worship the God of the Ebrewes: we pray thee, let us goe three daies journey in the desert, and sacrifice unto the Lord our God, least he bring upon us the pestilence or sword.
5.4: Then said the King of Egypt unto them, Moses and Aaron, why cause ye the people to cease from their workes? get you to your burdens.
5.5: Pharaoh said furthermore, Behold, much people is now in the land, and ye make them leave their burdens.
5.6: Therefore Pharaoh gave commandement the same day unto the taskemasters of the people, and to their officers, saying,
5.7: Ye shall give the people no more straw, to make brick ( as in time past) but let them goe and gather them straw them selves:
5.8: Notwithstanding lay upon them the nober of brick, which they made in time past, diminish nothing thereof: for they be idle, therefore they crie, saying, Let us go to offer sacrifice unto our God.
5.9: Lay more work upon the men, and cause them to do it, and let the not regard vain words.
5.10: Then went the taskemasters of the people and their officers out, and told the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will give you no more straw.
5.11: Goe your selves, get you straw where yee can find it, yet shall nothing of your labour bee diminished.
5.12: Then were the people scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt, for to gather stubble in stead of straw.
5.13: And the taskemasters hasted them, saying, Finish your dayes work every dayes task, as ye did when ye had straw.
5.14: And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaohs taskemasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick yesterday and to day, as in times past?
5.15: Then the officers of the children of Israel came, and cryed unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherfore dealest thou thus with thy servants?
5.16: There is no straw given to thy seruantes, and they say unto us, Make brick: and loe, thy servants are beaten, and thy people is blamed.
5.17: But he said, Ye are to much idle: therfore ye say, Let us goe to offer sacrifice to the Lord.
5.18: Goe therefore now and work: for there shall no straw be given you, yet shall yee deliver the whole tale of brick.
5.19: Then the officers of the children of Israel saw them selves in an evil case, because it was said, Ye shall diminish nothing of your brick, nor of every dayes task.
5.20: And they met Moses and Aaron, which stood in their way as they came out from Pharaoh,
5.21: To whom they said, The Lord look upon you and judge: for yee have made our sauour to stink before Pharaoh and before his servants, in that ye have put a sword in their hand to slay us.
5.22: Wherefore Moses returned to the Lord, and said, Lord, why hast thou afflicted this people? wherefore hast thou thus sent me?
5.23: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy Name, he hath vexed this people, and yet thou hast not delivered thy people.

6.1: Then the Lord sayd unto Moses, Now shalt thou see, what I will doe unto Pharaoh: for by a strong hand shall he let them goe, and even be constrained to drive them out of his land.
6.2: Moreover God spake unto Moses, and sayd unto him, I am the Lord,
6.3: And I appeared unto Abraham, to Izhak, and to Iaakob by the Name of Almightie God: but by my Name Jehovah was I not knowen unto the.
6.4: Furthermore as I made my covenant with them to give them ye land of Canaan, the land of their pilgrimage, wherein they were strangers:
6.5: So I have also heard the groning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and have remembred my covenant.
6.6: Wherefore say thou unto the children of Israel, I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from the burdens of the Egyptians, and will deliver you out of their bondage, and will redeem you in a stretched out arm, and in great iudgements.
6.7: Also I will take you for my people, and will be your God: then ye shall know that I the Lord your God bring you out from the burdens of the Egyptians.
6.8: And I will bring you into the land which I sware that I would give to Abraham, to Izhak, and to Iaakob, and I will give it unto you for a possession: I am the Lord.
6.9: So Moses told the children of Israel thus: but they hearkened not unto Moses, for anguish of spirit and for cruel bondage.
6.10: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.11: Go speak to Pharaoh King of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel goe out of his land.
6.12: But Moses spake before the Lord, saying, Behold, the children of Israel hearken not unto me, how then shall Pharaoh hear mee, which am of uncircumcised lippes?
6.13: Then the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and charged them to goe to the children of Israel and to Pharaoh King of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
6.14: These bee the heades of their fathers houses: the sonnes of Reuben the first borne of Israel are Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi: these are ye families of Reuben.
6.15: Also the sonnes of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zoar, and Shaul the sonne of a Canaanitish woman: these are the families of Simeon.
6.16: These also are the names of the sonnes of Levi in their generations: Gershon and Kohath and Merari (and the yeres of the life of Levi were an hundreth thirtie and seven yere)
6.17: The sonnes of Gershon were Libni and Shimi by their families.
6.18: And the sonnes of Kohath, Amram and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel. (and Kohath lived an hundreth thirtie and three yeere)
6.19: Also the sonnes of Merari were Mahali and Mushi: these are ye families of Levi by their kinreds.
6.20: And Amram took Jochebed his fathers sister to his wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses (and Amram lived an hundreth thirtie and seven yeere)
6.21: Also the sonnes of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
6.22: And the sonnes of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
6.23: And Aaron took Elisheba daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahashon to his wife, which bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
6.24: Also the sonnes of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these are the families of the Korhites.
6.25: And Eleazar Aarons sonne took him one of the daughters of Putiel to his wife, which bare him Phinehas: these are the principal fathers of the Levites throughout their families.
6.26: These are Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, Bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, according to their armies.
6.27: These are that Moses and Aaron, which spake to Pharaoh King of Egypt, that they might bring the children of Israel out of Egypt.
6.28: And at that time when the Lord spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt,
6.29: When the Lord, I say, spake unto Moses, saying, I am the Lord, speak thou unto Pharaoh the King of Egypt all that I say unto thee,
6.30: Then Moses said before the Lord, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh hear me?

7.1: Then the Lord said to Moses, Behold, I have made thee Pharaohs God, and Aaron thy brother shall be thy Prophet.
7.2: Thou shalt speak all that I commanded thee: and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he suffer the children of Israel to go out of his land.
7.3: But I will harden Pharaohs heart, and multiplie my miracles and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
7.4: And Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay mine hand upon Egypt, and bring out myne armies, even my people, the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, by great iudgements.
7.5: Then the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I stretch foorth mine hand upon Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.
7.6: So Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded them, even so did they.
7.7: (Now Moses was four score yeere old, and Aaron four score and three, when they spake unto Pharaoh)
7.8: And the Lord had spoken unto Moses and Aaron, saying,
7.9: If Pharaoh speak unto you, saying, Shew a miracle for you, then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shalbe turned into a serpent.
7.10: Then went Moses and Aaron unto Pharaoh, and did even as the Lord had commanded: and Aaron cast forth his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it was turned into a serpent.
7.11: Then Pharaoh called also for the wise men and sorcerers: and those charmers also of Egypt did in like maner with their enchantmens,
7.12: For they cast down every man his rod, and they were turned into serpents: but Aarons rod deuoured their rods.
7.13: So Pharaohs heart was hardened, and hee hearkened not to them, as the Lord had said.
7.14: The Lord then said unto Moses, Pharaohs heart is obstinate, hee refuseth to let the people goe.
7.15: Goe unto Pharaoh in the morning, (loe, he will come forth unto the water) and thou shalt stand and meet him by the rivers brink, and the rod, which was turned into a serpent, shalt thou take in thine hand.
7.16: And thou shalt say unto him, The Lord God of the Ebrewes hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people goe, that they may serve mee in the wilderness: and behold, hitherto thou wouldest not hear.
7.17: Thus saith the Lord, In this shalt thou know that I am the Lord: behold, I wil smite with the rod that is in mine hand upon the water that is in the river, and it shalbe turned to blood.
7.18: And the fish that is in the river shall dye, and the river shall stink, and it shall grieve the Egyptians to drink of the water of the river.
7.19: The Lord then spake to Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand over the waters of Egypt, over their streames, over their rivers, and over their pondes,, and over all pooles of their waters, and they shalbe blood, and there shalbe blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and of stone.
7.20: So Moses and Aaron did even as the Lord commanded: and hee lift up the rod, and smote the water that was in the river in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants: and all the water that was in the river, was turned into blood.
7.21: And the fish that was in the ryuer dyed, and the river stank: so that the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river: and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
7.22: And the enchanters of Egypt did likewise with their sorceries: and the heart of Phraoh was hardened: so that he did not hearken unto them, as the Lord had sayde.
7.23: Then Pharaoh returned, and went again into his house, neither did this yet enter into his heart.
7.24: All the Egyptians then digged round about the river for waters to drink: for they could not drink of the water of the river.
7.25: And this continued fully seven dayes after the Lord had smitten the river.

8.1: Afterward the Lord sayde unto Moses, Goe unto Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith the Lord, Let my people goe, that they may serve me:
8.2: And if thou wilt not let them goe, behold, I will smite all thy countrey with frogges:
8.3: And the river shall scral ful of frogges, which shall goe up and come into thine house, and into thy chamber, where thou sleepest, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneading troughes.
8.4: Yea, the frogges shall climb up upon thee, and on thy people, and upon all thy servants.
8.5: Also the Lord said unto Moses, Say thou unto Aaron, Stretch out thine hand with thy rod upon the streames, upon the rivers, and upon the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.
8.6: Then Aaron stretched out his hand upon the waters of Egypt, and the frogges came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
8.7: And the sorcerers did likewise with their sorceries, and brought frogges up upon the land of Egypt.
8.8: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Pray ye unto the Lord, that hee may take away the frogges from mee, and from my people, and I will let the people goe, that they may doe sacrifice unto the Lord.
8.9: And Moses said unto Pharaoh, Concerning me, even command when I shall pray for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to destroy the frogges from thee and from thine houses, that they may remain in the river only.
8.10: Then he said, To morowe. And he answered, Be it as thou hast said, that thou maiest know, that there is none like unto the Lord our God.
8.11: So the frogges shall depart from thee, and from thine houses, and from thy seruantes, and from thy people: onely they shall remain in the river.
8.12: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh: and Moses cryed unto the Lord concerning the frogges, which hee had sent unto Pharaoh.
8.13: And the Lord did according to the saying of Moses: so the frogges died in the houses, in the townes, and in the fieldes.
8.14: And they gathered the together by heaps, and the land stank of them.
8.15: But when Pharaoh saw that hee had rest given him, he hardened his heart, and hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had said.
8.16: Again the Lord sayd unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out the rod, and smite the dust of the earth, that it may bee turned to lyce throughout all the land of Egypt.
8.17: And they did so: for Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth: and lyce came upon man and upon beast: all the dust of the earth was lyce throughout all the land of Egypt.
8.18: Now the enchanters assaied likewise with their enchantments to bring forth lyce, but they could not. So the lyce were upon man and upon beast.
8.19: Then said the enchanters unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God. But Pharaohs heart remained obstinate, and hee hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had said.
8.20: Moreover the Lord sayd to Moses, Rise up earely in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh (lo, hee will come forth unto the water) and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
8.21: Els, if thou wilt not let my people goe, behold, I will send swarmes of flies both upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine houses: and the houses of the Egyptians shalbe full of swarmes of flies, and the ground also whereon they are.
8.22: But ye land of Goshe, where my people are, wil I cause to be wonderful in that day, so that no swarmes of flies shalbe there, that thou maiest know that I am the Lord in the middes of the earth.
8.23: And I will make a deliverance of my people from thy people: to morowe shall this miracle be.
8.24: And the Lord did so: for there came great swarmes of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants houses, so that through all the land of Egypt, the earth was corrupt by the swarmes of flies.
8.25: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Goe, doe sacrifice unto your God in this land.
8.26: But Moses answered, It is not meet to do so: for then we should offer unto the Lord our God that, which is an abomination unto the Egyptians. Loe, can we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and they not stone us?
8.27: Let us go three dayes journey in the desert, and sacrifice unto the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.
8.28: And Pharaoh said, I will let you go, that ye may sacrifice unto the Lord your God in the wilderness: but goe not far away, pray for me.
8.29: And Moses said, Behold, I will go out from thee, and pray unto the Lord, that the swarmes of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people to morowe: but let Pharaoh from hencefoorth deceive no more, in not suffering the people to sacrifice unto the Lord.
8.30: So Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed unto the Lord.
8.31: And the Lord did according to the saying of Moses, and the swarmes of flies departed from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, and there remained not one.
8.32: Yet Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and did not let the people goe.

9.1: Then the Lord said unto Moses, Go to Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Ebrewes, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
9.2: But if thou refuse to let them goe, and wilt yet hold them still,
9.3: Behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thy flock which is in the field: for upon the horses, upon the asses, upon the camels, upon the cattell, and upon the sheep shalbe a mightie great moraine.
9.4: And the Lord shall doe wonderfully between the beastes of Israel, and the beastes of Egypt: so that there shall nothing dye of all, that pertaineth to the children of Israel.
9.5: And the Lord appointed a time, saying, To morowe the Lord shall finish this thing in this land.
9.6: So the Lord did this thing on the morow, and all the cattel of Egypt dyed: but of the cattell of the children of Israel dyed not one.
9.7: Then Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattell of the Israelites dead: and the heart of Pharaoh was obstinate, and hee did not let the people goe.
9.8: And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron, Take your handful of ashes of the fornace, and Moses shall sprinkle them toward the heaven in the sight of Pharaoh,
9.9: And they shall be turned to dust in all the land of Egypt: and it shalbe as a scab breaking out into blisters upon man, and upon beast, thorow out all the land of Egypt.
9.10: Then they took ashes of the fornace, and stood before Pharaoh: and Moses sprinkled them toward the heaven, and there came a scab breaking out into blisters upon man, and upon beast.
9.11: And the sorcerers could not stand before Moses, because of the scab: for the scab was upon the enchanters, and upon all the Egyptians.
9.12: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had said unto Moses.
9.13: Also the Lord said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Ebrewes, Let my people goe, that they may serve me.
9.14: For I will at this time send all my plagues upon thine heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people, that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.
9.15: For now I will stretch out mine hand, that I may smite thee and thy people with the pestilence: and thou shalt perish from the earth.
9.16: And in deed, for this cause have I appointed thee, to shew my power in thee, and to declare my Name throughout all the world.
9.17: Yet thou exaltest thy self against my people, and lettest them not goe.
9.18: Behold, to morowe this time I will cause to rain a mightie great hail, such as was not in Egypt since the foundation thereof was laid unto this time.
9.19: Send therefore now, and gather the cattell, and all that thou hast in the field: for upon all the men, and the beastes, which are found in the field, and not brought home, the hail shall fall upon them, and they shall die.
9.20: Such then as feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh, made his servants and his cattell flee into the houses:
9.21: But such as regarded not the word of the Lord, left his servants, and his cattell in the field.
9.22: And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch foorth thine hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, upon man, and upon beast, and upon all the herbes of the field in the land of Egypt.
9.23: Then Moses stretched out his rod toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightening upon the ground: and the Lord caused hail to rain upon the land of Egypt.
9.24: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, so grieuous, as there was none throughout all the land of Egypt, since it was a nation.
9.25: And the hail smote throughout al ye land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast: also ye hail smote all the herbes of ye field, and brake to pieces all the trees of the field.
9.26: Onely in the land of Goshen (where the children of Israel were) was no hail.
9.27: Then Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have now sinned: the Lord is righteous, but I and my people are wicked.
9.28: Pray ye unto the Lord (for it is ynough) that there be no more mightie thunders and hail, and I will let you goe, and yee shall tarie no longer.
9.29: Then Moses said unto him, Assoone as I am out of the citie, I will spread mine hands unto the Lord, and the thunder shall cease, neither shall there be any more hail, that thou mayest know that the earth is the Lordes.
9.30: As for thee and thy servants, I know afore I pray ye will fear before the face of the Lord God.
9.31: (And the flax, and the barley were smitten: for the barley was eared, and the flax was bolled.
9.32: But the wheat and the rye were not smitten, for they were hid in the ground)
9.33: Then Moses went out of the citie from Pharaoh, and spred his hands to the Lord, and the thunder and the hail ceased, neither rained it upon the earth.
9.34: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder were ceased, hee sinned again, and hardened his heart, both he, and his servants.
9.35: So the heart of Pharaoh was hardened: neither would he let the children of Israel goe, as the Lord had said by Moses.

10.1: Again the Lord said unto Moses, Goe to Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might work these my miracles in the middes of his realm,
10.2: And that thou maist declare in the eares of thy sonne, and of thy sonnes sonne, what things I have done in Egypt, and my miracles, which I have done among them: that ye may know that I am the Lord.
10.3: Then came Moses and Aaron unto Pharaoh, and they said unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Ebrewes, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thy self before me? Let my people goe, that they may serve me.
10.4: But if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to morowe will I bring grashoppers into thy coastes.
10.5: And they shall cover the face of the earth, that a man can not see the earth: and they shall eat the residue which remaineth unto you, and hath escaped from the hail: and they shall eat all your trees that bud in the field.
10.6: And they shall fil thine houses, and all thy servants houses, and the houses of all the Egyptians, as neither thy fathers, nor thy fathers fathers have seen, since the time they were upon the earth unto this day. So he returned, and went out from Pharaoh.
10.7: Then Pharaohs servants said unto him, How long shall he be an offence unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the Lord their God: wilt thou first know that Egypt is destroyed?
10.8: So Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh, and he said unto them, Goe, serve the Lord your God, but who are they that shall goe?
10.9: And Moses answered, We will go with our yong and with our old, with our sonnes and with our daughters, with our sheep and with our cattell will we goe: for we must celebrate a feast unto the Lord.
10.10: And he said unto them, Let the Lord so be with you, as I will let you goe and your children: behold, for evil is before your face.
10.11: It shall not be so: now goe ye that are men, and serve the Lord: for that was your desire. Then they were thrust out from Pharaohs presence.
10.12: After, the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand upon the land of Egypt for the grashoppers, that they may come upon the land of Egypt, and eat all the herbes of the land, even all that the hail hath left.
10.13: Then Moses stretched foorth his rod upon the land of Egypt: and the Lord brought an East wind upon the land all that day, and al that night: and in the morning the East wind brought the grashoppers.
10.14: So the grashoppers went up upon all the land of Egypt, and remained in all quarters of Egypt: so grieuous Grashoppers, like to these were never before, neither after them shalbe such.
10.15: For they covered all the face of the earth, so that the land was dark: and they did eat all the herbes of the land, and all the fruites of the trees, which the hail had left, so that there was no green thing left upon the trees, nor among the herbes of the field throughout all the land of Egypt.
10.16: Therefore Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste, and sayde, I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you.
10.17: And now forgive mee my sinne onely this once, and pray unto the Lord your God, that hee may take away from me this death onely.
10.18: Moses then went out from Pharaoh, and prayed unto the Lord.
10.19: And the Lord turned a mightie strong West wind, and took away the grashoppers, and violently cast them into the red Sea, so that there remained not one grashopper in all the coast of Egypt.
10.20: But the Lord hardened Pharaohs heart, and hee did not let the children of Israel goe.
10.21: Again ye Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be upon the land of Egypt darkenesse, even darkenesse that may be felt.
10.22: Then Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven, and there was a black darkenesse in all the land of Egypt three daies.
10.23: No man saw an other, neither rose up from ye place where he was for three dayes: but all the children of Israel had light where they dwelt.
10.24: The Pharaoh called for Moses and said, Go, serve the Lord: onely your sheep and your cattel shall abide, and your children shall go with you.
10.25: And Moses sayd, Thou must give us also sacrifices, and burnt offrings that wee may doe sacrifice unto the Lord our God.
10.26: Therefore our cattell also shall go with us: there shall not an hoof bee left, for thereof must we take to serve the Lord our God: neither doe wee know how we shall serve the Lord, until we come thither.
10.27: (But the Lord hardened Pharaohs heart, and he would not let them goe)
10.28: And Pharaoh sayde unto him, Get thee from mee: look thou see my face no more: for whensoever thou comest in my sight, thou shalt dye.
10.29: Then Moses said, Thou hast said well: from henceforth will I see thy face no more.

11.1: Now the Lord had said unto Moses, yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt: after that, he will let you go hence: when he letteth you goe, he shall at once chase you hence.
11.2: Speak thou now to the people, that every man require of his neighbour, and every woman of her neighbour jewels of silver and jewels of gold.
11.3: And the Lord gave the people fauour in the sight of the Egyptians: also Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaohs seruantes, and in the sight of the people.)
11.4: Also Moses sayde, Thus sayth the Lord, About midnight will I goe out into the middes of Egypt.
11.5: And all the first borne in the land of Egypt shall die, from the first borne of Pharaoh that sitteth on his throne, unto the first borne of the maid servant, that is at the mille, and all the first borne of beastes.
11.6: Then there shalbe a great crie throughout all the land of Egypt, such as was never none like, nor shalbe.
11.7: But against none of ye children of Israel shall a dogge move his tongue, neyther against man nor beast, that ye may know that the Lord putteth a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.
11.8: And all these thy servants shall come down unto me, and fal before me, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that are at thy feet, and after this will I depart. So he went out from Pharaoh very angry.
11.9: And the Lord said unto Moses, Pharaoh shall not hear you, that my wonders may bee multiplied in the land of Egypt.
11.10: So Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh: but the Lord hardened Pharaohs heart, and he suffred not the children of Israel to goe out of his land.

12.1: Then the Lord spake to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
12.2: This moneth shalbe unto you the beginning of moneths: it shalbe to you the first moneth of the yere.
12.3: Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth of this moneth let every man take unto him a lamb, according to the house of the fathers, a lamb for an house.
12.4: And if the housholde be too litle for the lamb, he shall take his neighbour, which is next unto his house, according to the nomber of the persons: every one of you, according to his eating shall make your count for the lambes,
12.5: Your lamb shalbe without blemish, a male of a yeere old: ye shall take it of the lambes, or of the kiddes.
12.6: And yee shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this moneth: then al the multitude of the Congregation of Israel shall kill it at even.
12.7: After, they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two postes, and on the upper door post of the houses where they shall eat it.
12.8: And they shall eat the flesh the same night, roste with fire, and vnleauened bread: with sowre herbes they shall eat it.
12.9: Eat not thereof raw, boyled nor sodden in water, but rost with fire, both his head, his feet, and his purtenance.
12.10: And ye shall reserve nothing of it unto the morning: but that, which remaineth of it unto the morowe, shall ye burn with fire.
12.11: And thus shall yee eat it, Your loynes girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staves in your handes, and yee shall eat it in haste: for it is the Lords Passeouer.
12.12: For I will pass through the land of Egypt the same night, and will smite all the first borne in the land of Egypt, both man and beast, and I will execute iudgement upon all the gods of Egypt. I am the Lord.
12.13: And the blood shalbe a token for you upon the houses where ye are: so when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destruction, when I smite the land of Egypt.
12.14: And this day shalbe unto you a remembrance: and ye shall keep it an holie feast unto the Lord, throughout your generations: yee shall keep it holie by an ordinance for ever.
12.15: Seven daies shall ye eat vnleauened bread, and in any case ye shall put away leaven the first day out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first daie until the seventh day, that person shalbe cut off from Israel.
12.16: And in the first day shalbe an holie assemblie: also in the seventh day shalbe an holy assemblie unto you: no work shalbe done in them, save about that which every man must eat: that onely may ye do.
12.17: Ye shall keep also the feast of vnleauened bread: for that same day I will bring your armies out of the land of Egypt: therefore ye shall observe this day, throughout your posteritie, by an ordinance for ever.
12.18: In the first moneth and the fourteenth day of the moneth at even, yee shall eat vnleauened bread unto the one and twentieth day of the moneth at even.
12.19: Seven daies shall no leaven be found in your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread, that person shalbe cut off from the Congregation of Israel: whether he bee a stranger, or borne in the land.
12.20: Ye shall eat no leavened bread: but in all your habitations shall ye eat vnleauened bread.
12.21: Then Moses called all the Elders of Israel, and said unto them, Choose out and take you for euerie of your housholdes a lamb, and kill the Passeouer.
12.22: And take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basen, and strike the lintel, and the door cheekes with the blood that is in the basen, and let none of you goe out at the door of his house, until the morning.
12.23: For the Lord will pass by to smite the Egyptians: and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel and on the two door cheekes, the Lord wil pass over the door, and wil not suffer the destroyer to come into your houses to plague you.
12.24: Therefore shall ye observe this thing as an ordinance both for thee and thy sonnes for ever.
12.25: And when ye shall come into the land, which the Lord will give you as hee hath promised, then ye shall keep this service.
12.26: And when your children ask you, What service is this ye keep?
12.27: Then ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of the Lordes Passeouer, which passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and preserved our houses. Then the people bowed them selves, and worshipped.
12.28: So the children of Israel went, and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron: so did they.
12.29: Now at midnight, the Lord smote all the first borne in the land of Egypt, from the first borne of Pharaoh that sat on his throne, unto the first borne of the captive that was in prison, and all the first borne of beastes.
12.30: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants and all the Egyptians: and there was a great cry in Egypt: for there was no house where there was not one dead.
12.31: And hee called to Moses and to Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, get you out from among my people, both yee, and the children of Israel, and goe serve the Lord as ye have sayde.
12.32: Take also your sheep and your cattell as yee have sayde, and depart, and bless me also.
12.33: And the Egyptians did force the people, because they would send them out of the land in haste: for they said, We die all.
12.34: Therfore the people took their dough before it was leavened, even their dough bound in clothes upon their shoulders.
12.35: And the children of Israel did according to the saying of Moses, and they asked of ye Egyptians jewels of silver and jewels of gold, and raiment.
12.36: And the Lord gave the people fauour in the sight of the Egyptians: and they graunted their request: so they spoyled the Egyptians.
12.37: Then the children of Israel took their journey from Rameses to Succoth about six hundreth thousand men of foot, beside children.
12.38: And a great multitude of sundrie sortes of people went out with them, and sheep, and beeves, and cattel in great abundance.
12.39: And they baked the dough which they brought out of Egypt, and made vnleauened cakes: for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, neither could they tarie, nor yet prepare themselves vitailes.
12.40: So the dwelling of the children of Israel, while they dwelled in Egypt, was four hundreth and thirtie yeres.
12.41: And when the four hundreth and thirtie yeeres were expired, even the self same day departed all the hostes of the Lord out of the land of Egypt.
12.42: It is a night to be kept holie to the Lord, because he brought them out of the land of Egypt: this is that night of the Lord, which all the children of Israel must keep throughout their generations.
12.43: Also the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the Law of the Passeouer: no stranger shall eat thereof.
12.44: But euerie servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.
12.45: A stranger or an hyred servant shall not eat thereof.
12.46: In one house shall it bee eaten: thou shalt carie none of ye flesh out of the house, neither shall ye break a bone thereof.
12.47: All the Congregation of Israel shall observe it.
12.48: But if a stranger dwell with thee, and will observe the Passeouer of the Lord, let him circumcise all the males, that belong unto him, and then let him come and observe it, and he shall be as one that is borne in the land: for none uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.
12.49: One law shalbe to him that is borne in the land, and to the stranger that dwelleth among you.
12.50: Then all the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron: so did they.
12.51: And the self same day did the Lord bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

13.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
13.2: Sanctifie unto me all the first borne: that is, every one that first openeth the womb among the children of Israel, as well of man as of beast: for it is mine.
13.3: Then Moses sayd unto the people, Remember this day in the which ye came out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage: for by a mightie hand the Lord brought you out from thence: therefore no leavened bread shall bee eaten.
13.4: This day come yee out in the moneth of Abib.
13.5: Now when the Lord hath brought thee into the land of the Canaanites, and Hittites, and Amorites, and Hivites, and Jebusites (which he sware unto thy fathers, that he would give thee, a land flowing with milk and honie) then thou shalt keep this service in this moneth.
13.6: Seven dayes shalt thou eat vnleauened bread, and the seventh day shall be the feast of the Lord.
13.7: Vnleauened bread shall bee eaten seven dayes, and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, nor yet leaven be seen with thee in all thy quarters.
13.8: And thou shalt shew thy sonne in that day, saying, This is done, because of that which the Lord did unto me, when I came out of Egypt.
13.9: And it shalbe a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a remembrance between thine eyes, that the Law of the Lord may be in thy mouth: for by a strong hand the Lord brought thee out of Egypt.
13.10: Keep therefore this ordinance in his season appoynted from yeere to yeere.
13.11: And when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, as hee sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,
13.12: Then thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that first openeth the womb: also every thing that first doeth open the womb, and cometh forth of thy beast: the males shalbe the Lordes.
13.13: But every first foal of an ass, thou shalt redeem with a lamb: and if thou redeem him not, then thou shalt break his neck: likewise all the first borne of man among thy sonnes shalt thou bye out.
13.14: And when thy sonne shall ask thee to morowe, saying, What is this? thou shalt then say unto him, With a mightie hand the Lord brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
13.15: For when Pharaoh was hard hearted against our departing, the Lord then slew all the first borne in the land of Egypt: from the first borne of man even to the first borne of beast: therefore I sacrifice unto the Lord all the males that first open the womb, but all the first borne of my sonnes I redeem.
13.16: And it shalbe as a token upon thine hand, and as frontlets between thine eyes, that the Lord brought us out of Egypt by a mightie hand.
13.17: Now when Pharaoh had let the people go, God caried them not by the way of the Philistims countrey, though it were neerer: (for God sayd, Lest the people repent whe they see war, and turn again to Egypt)
13.18: But God made the people to go about by the way of the wilderness of the red sea: and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.
13.19: (And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had made the children of Israel swear, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall take my bones away hence with you)
13.20: So they took their journey from Succoth, and camped in Etham in the edge of the wilderness.
13.21: And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, that they might go both by day and by night.
13.22: He took not away the pillar of ye cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night from before the people.

14.1: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
14.2: Speak to the children of Israel, that they return and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the Sea, over against Baal-zephon: about it shall ye camp by the Sea.
14.3: For Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are tangled in the land: the wilderness hath shut them in.
14.4: And I will harden Pharaohs heart that hee shall follow after you: so I will get mee honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host: the Egyptians also shall know that I am the Lord: and they did so.
14.5: Then it was told the King of Egypt, that the people fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they sayde, Why have we this done, and have let Israel go out of our service?
14.6: And he made ready his charets, and took his people with him,
14.7: And took six hundreth chosen charets, and all the charets of Egypt, and captaines over every one of them.
14.8: (For the Lord had hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he followed after the children of Israel: but the children of Israel went out with an hie hand)
14.9: And the Egyptians pursued after them, and all the horses and charets of Pharaoh, and his horsemen and his host overtook them camping by the Sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
14.10: And when Pharaoh drew nie, the children of Israel lift up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians marched after them, and they were sore afrayde: wherefore the children of Israel cried unto the Lord.
14.11: And they sayde unto Moses, Hast thou brought us to die in the wildernes, because there were no graves in Egypt? wherefore hast thou served us thus, to carie us out of Egypt?
14.12: Did not wee tell thee this thing in Egypt, saying, Let us be in rest, that we may serve the Egyptians? for it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, then that wee should dye in the wilderness.
14.13: Then Moses sayde to the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and behold the salvation of the Lord which he will shew to you this day. For the Egyptians, whom ye have seen this day, ye shall never see them again.
14.14: The Lord shall fight for you: therefore hold you your peace.
14.15: And the Lord sayd unto Moses, Wherefore cryest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel that they go forward:
14.16: And lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the Sea and deuide it, and let the children of Israel goe on drie ground thorow the middes of the Sea.
14.17: And I, behold, I will harden the heart of the Egyptians, that they may follow them, and I wil get me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his charets, and upon his horsemen.
14.18: Then the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I have gotten me honour upon Pharaoh, upon his charets, and upon his horsemen.
14.19: (And the Angel of God, which went before the host of Israel, removed and went behind them: also the pillar of the cloud went from before them, and stood behind them,
14.20: And came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel: it was both a cloud and darkenes, yet gave it light by night, so that all the night long the one came not at the other)
14.21: And Moses stretched forth his hand upon the Sea, and the Lord caused the sea to runne back by a strong East wind all the night, and made the Sea dry land: for the waters were deuided.
14.22: Then the children of Israel went through the middes of the Sea upon the drie ground, and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left hand.
14.23: And the Egyptians pursued and went after them to the middes of the Sea, even all Pharaohs horses, his charets, and his horsemen.
14.24: Now in the morning watch, when the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians, out of the firie and cloudie pillar, he strooke the host of the Egyptians with fear.
14.25: For he took off their charet wheeles, and they drave them with much a doe: so that the Egyptians every one sayd, I wil flee from the face of Israel: for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.
14.26: Then the Lord sayde to Moses, Stretch thine hand upon the Sea, that the waters may return upon the Egyptians, upon their charets and upon their horsemen.
14.27: Then Moses stretched forth his hand upon the Sea, and the Sea returned to his force early in the morning, and the Egyptians fled against it: but the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the mids of the Sea.
14.28: So the water returned and covered the charets and the horsemen, even all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them: there remained not one of them.
14.29: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land thorowe the middes of the Sea, and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
14.30: Thus the Lord saved Israel the same day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the Sea bank.
14.31: And Israel saw the mightie power, which the Lord shewed upon the Egyptians: so the people feared the Lord, and beleeued the Lord, and his servant Moses.

15.1: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the Lord, and sayd in this maner, I will sing unto the Lord: for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and him that rode upon him hath he ouerthrowen in the Sea.
15.2: The Lord is my strength and praise, and he is become my salvation. He is my God, and I will prepare him a tabernacle. he is my fathers God, and I will exalt him.
15.3: The Lord is a man of war, his Name is Jehovah.
15.4: Pharaohs charets and his host hath he cast into the Sea: his chosen captaines also were drowned in the red Sea.
15.5: The depths have covered them, they sank to the bottom as a stone.
15.6: Thy right hand, O Lord, is glorious in power: thy right hand, O Lord, hath brused the enemie.
15.7: And in thy great glorie thou hast ouerthrowen them that rose against thee: thou sentest forth thy wrath, which consumed them as the stubble.
15.8: And by the blast of thy nostrels the waters were gathered, the floods stood still as an heap, the depthes congealed together in the heart of the Sea.
15.9: The enemie sayd, I wil pursue, I wil overtake them, I will deuide the spoyle, my lust shall bee satisfied upon them, I will draw my sword, mine hand shall destroy them.
15.10: Thou blewest with thy wind, the Sea covered them, they sank as lead in the mightie waters.
15.11: Who is like unto thee, O Lord, among the Gods! who is like thee so glorious in holiness, fearefull in prayses, doing wonders!
15.12: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them.
15.13: Thou wilt by thy mercie cary this people, which thou deliveredst: thou wilt bring them in thy strength unto thine holy habitation.
15.14: The people shall hear and be afraid: sorow shall come upon the inhabitants of Palestina.
15.15: Then the dukes of Edom shalbe amased, and trembling shall come upon the great men of Moab: all the inhabitantes of Canaan shall wax faint hearted.
15.16: Fear and dread shall fall upon them: because of the greatness of thine arm, they shalbe stil as a stone, till thy people pass, O Lord: til this people pass, which thou hast purchased.
15.17: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, which is the place that thou hast prepared, O Lord, for to dwell in, even the sanctuarie, O Lord, which thine hands shall establish.
15.18: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.
15.19: For Pharaohs horses went with his charets and horsemen into the Sea, and the Lord brought the waters of the Sea upon them: but the children of Israel went on drie land in the middes of the Sea.
15.20: And Miriam the prophetess, sister of Aaron took a timbrel in her hand, and all the women came out after her with timbrels and daunces.
15.21: And Miriam answered the men, Sing yee unto the Lord: for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath hee ouerthrowen in the Sea.
15.22: Then Moses brought Israel from the redde Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur: and they went three dayes in the wilderness, and found no waters.
15.23: And whe they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of the place was called Marah.
15.24: Then the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
15.25: And he cried unto the Lord, and the Lord shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were sweet: there he made them an ordinance and a law, and there he proved them,
15.26: And sayd, if thou wilt diligently hearken, O Israel, unto the voyce of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that, which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear unto his commandements, and keep all his ordinances, then will I put none of these diseases upon thee, which I brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.
15.27: And they came to Elim, where were twelve fountaines of water, and seuentie palm trees, and they camped thereby the waters.

16.1: Afterward all the Congregation of the children of Israel departed from Elim, and came to the wildernes of Sin, (which is between Elim and Sinai) the fiftenth day of the second moneth after their departing out of ye land of Egypt.
16.2: And the whole Congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.
16.3: For the children of Israel sayde to them, Oh that we had dyed by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when wee sat by the flesh pots, when wee ate bread our bellies full: for yee have brought us out into this wilderness, to kill this whole company with famine.
16.4: Then sayd the Lord unto Moses, Behold, I wil cause bread to rayne from heaven to you, and the people shall goe out, and gather that that is sufficient for every day, that I may prove them, whether they wil walk in my Law or no.
16.5: But the sixt day they shall prepare that, which they shall bring home, and it shalbe twise as much as they gather dayly.
16.6: Then Moses and Aaron sayde unto all the children of Israel, At even ye shall know, that the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt:
16.7: And in the morning ye shall see the glorie of the Lord: for he hath heard your grudgings against the Lord: and what are we that ye have murmured against us?
16.8: Again Moses sayd, At even shall the Lord give you flesh to eat, and in the morning your fil of bread: for the Lord hath heard your murmurings, which ye murmur against him: for what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord.
16.9: And Moses sayd to Aaron, Say unto all the Congregation of the children of Israel, Draw neere before the Lord: for he hath heard your murmurings.
16.10: Now as Aaron spake unto the whole Congregation of the children of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.
16.11: (For the Lord had spoken unto Moses, saying,
16.12: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: tell them therefore, and say, At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread, and ye shall know that I am the Lord your God)
16.13: And so at even the quailes came and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host.
16.14: And when the dew that was fallen was ascended, behold, a small round thing was upon the face of the wildernes, small as the hoar frost on the earth.
16.15: And when the children of Israel saw it, they sayde one to another, It is MAN, for they wist not what it was. And Moses sayd unto them, This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.
16.16: This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded: gather of it every man according to his eating an Omer for a man according to the number of your persons: every man shall take for them which are in his tent.
16.17: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.
16.18: And when they did measure it with an Omer, hee that had gathered much, had nothing over, and he that had gathered litle, had no lack: so every man gathered according to his eating.
16.19: Moses then said unto them, Let no man reserve thereof till morning.
16.20: Notwithstanding they obeyed not Moses: but some of them reserved of it till morning, and it was full of wormes, and stank: therefore Moses was angrie with them.
16.21: And they gathered it every morning, every man according to his eating: for when the heat of the sunne came, it was melted.
16.22: And the sixt day they gathered twise so much bread, two Omers for one man: then all the rulers of the Congregation came and told Moses.
16.23: And he answered them, This is that, which the Lord hath sayde, To morowe is the rest of the holy Sabbath unto the Lord: bake that to day which ye wil bake, and seethe that which ye wil seethe, and all that remaineth, lay it up to be kept till the morning for you.
16.24: And they laied it up till the morning, as Moses bade, and it stank not, neyther was there any worm therein.
16.25: Then Moses sayde, Eat that to day: for to day is the Sabbath unto the Lord: to day ye shall not find it in the field.
16.26: Six dayes shall yee gather it, but in the seventh day is the Sabbath: in it there shalbe none.
16.27: Notwithstanding, there went out some of the people in ye seventh day for to gather, and they found none.
16.28: And the Lord sayde unto Moses, How long refuse yee to keep my commandements, and my lawes?
16.29: Behold, how the Lord hath given you the Sabbath: therefore he giveth you the sixt day bread for two dayes: tary therefore every man in his place: let no man goe out of his place the seventh day.
16.30: So the people rested the seventh day.
16.31: And the house of Israel called the name of it, MAN. and it was like to coriander seed, but white: and the taste of it was like unto wafers made with hony.
16.32: And Moses said, This is that which the Lord hath commanded, Fill an Omer of it, to keep it for your posteritie: that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.
16.33: Moses also said to Aaron, Take a pot and put an Omer full of MAN therein, and set it before the Lord to be kept for your posteritie.
16.34: As the Lord commanded Moses, so Aaron laied it up before the Testimonie to be kept.
16.35: And the children of Israel did eat MAN fourtie yeres, until they came unto a land inhabited: they did eat MAN until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan.
16.36: The Omer is the tenth part of the Ephah.

17.1: And all the Congregation of the children of Israel departed from the wilderness of Sin, by their iourneyes at the commandement of the Lord, and camped in Rephidim, where was no water for the people to drink.
17.2: Wherefore the people contended with Moses, and sayde, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses sayde unto them, Why contend yee with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?
17.3: So the people thirsted there for water, and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore hast thou thus brought us out of Egypt to kill us and our children and our cattel with thirst?
17.4: And Moses cried to the Lord, saying, What shall I do to this people? for they be almost ready to stone me.
17.5: And ye Lord answered to Moses, Goe before the people, and take with thee of the Elders of Israel: and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go:
17.6: Behold, I will stand there before thee upon the rock in Horeb, and thou shalt smite on the rock, and water shall come out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the Elders of Israel.
17.7: And he called the name of the place, Massah and Meribah, because of the contention of the children of Israel, and because they had tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or no?
17.8: Then came Amalek and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
17.9: And Moses sayde to Joshua, Chuse us out men, and go fight with Amalek: to morowe I will stand on the toppe of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.
17.10: So Joshua did as Moses bad him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur, went up to the top of the hill.
17.11: And when Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed: but when he let his hand down, Amalek prevailed.
17.12: Now Moses handes were heavy: therefore they took a stone and put it under him, and hee sat upon it: and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side: so his hands were steady until the going down of the sunne.
17.13: And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
17.14: And the Lord sayde to Moses, Write this for a remembrance in the book, and rehearse it to Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
17.15: (And Moses built an altar and called the name of it, Jehovah-nissi)
17.16: Also he said, The Lord hath sworn, that he will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

18.1: When Jethro the Priest of Midian Moses father in law heard all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, and how the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt,
18.2: Then Jethro the father in law of Moses, took Zipporah Moses wife, (after he had sent her away)
18.3: And her two sonnes, (whereof the one was called Gershom: for he sayd, I have been an aliant in a strange land:
18.4: And the name of the other was Eliezer: for the God of my father, said he, was mine help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh)
18.5: And Jethro Moses father in law came with his two sonnes, and his wife unto Moses into the wildernes, where he camped by ye mout of God.
18.6: And he said to Moses, I thy father in law Jethro am come to thee, and thy wife and her two sonnes with her.
18.7: And Moses went out to meet his father in law, and did obeisance and kissed him, and eche asked other of his welfare: and they came into the tent.
18.8: Then Moses told his father in law all that the Lord had done unto Pharaoh, and to the Egyptians for Israels sake, and all the travail that had come unto them by the way, and how the Lord delivered them.
18.9: And Jethro reioyced at all the goodness, which the Lord had shewed to Israel, and because he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians.
18.10: Therfore Jethro sayd, Blessed be the Lord who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh: who hath also delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
18.11: Now I know that the Lord is greater then all the gods: for as they have dealt proudly with them, so are they recompensed.
18.12: Then Jethro Moses father in law took burnt offerings and sacrifices to offer unto God. And Aaron and all the Elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses father in law before God.
18.13: Now on the morow, when Moses sat to judge the people, the people stood about Moses from morning unto even.
18.14: And when Moses father in law saw all that he did to the people, he sayde, What is this that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thy self alone, and all the people stand about thee from morning unto even?
18.15: And Moses sayd unto his father in law, Because the people come unto me to seek God.
18.16: When they have a matter, they come unto me, and I judge between one and another, and declare the ordinances of God, and his lawes.
18.17: But Moses father in law said unto him, The thing which thou doest, is not well.
18.18: Thou both weariest thy self greatly, and this people that is with thee: for the thing is too heauie for thee: thou art not able to doe it thy self alone.
18.19: Hear now my voyce, (I will give thee counsel, and God shalbe with thee) be thou for the people to Godwarde, and report thou the causes unto God,
18.20: And admonish them of the ordinances, and of the lawes, and shew them the way, wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.
18.21: Moreover, provide thou among al the people men of courage, fearing God, men dealing truely, hating couetousnesse: and appoynt such over them to be rulers over thousandes, rulers over hundreths, rulers over fifties, and rulers over tennes.
18.22: And let them judge the people at all seasons: but every great matter let them bring unto thee, and let them judge all small causes: so shall it be easier for thee, when they shall bear the burden with thee.
18.23: If thou do this thing, (and God so command thee) both thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go quietly to their place.
18.24: So Moses obeyed the voyce of his father in law, and did all that he had sayd:
18.25: And Moses chose men of courage out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers over thousandes, rulers over hundreths, rulers over fifties, and rulers over tennes.
18.26: And they judged the people at all seasons, but they brought the hard causes unto Moses: for they judged all small matters themselves.
18.27: Afterward Moses let his father in law depart, and he went into his countrey.

19.1: In the third moneth, after the children of Israel were gone out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they into the wildernes of Sinai.
19.2: For they departed from Rephidim, and came to the desart of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness: even there Israel camped before the mount.
19.3: But Moses went up unto God, for ye Lord had called out of the mount unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Iaakob, and tell the children of Israel,
19.4: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I caryed you upon eagles wings, and have brought you unto me.
19.5: Now therefore if ye wil hear my voyce in deed, and keep my covenant, then ye shalbe my chief treasure above all people, though all the earth be mine.
19.6: Yee shall be unto mee also a kingdom of Priestes, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.
19.7: Moses then came and called for the Elders of the people, and proposed unto them all these things, which the Lord commanded him.
19.8: And the people answered all together, and sayd, All that the Lord hath commanded, we will doe. And Moses reported the wordes of the people unto the Lord.
19.9: And the Lord sayd unto Moses, Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud, that the people may hear, whiles I talk with thee, and that they may also beleeue thee for ever. (for Moses had told the wordes of the people unto the Lord)
19.10: Moreover, the Lord sayd unto Moses, Goe to the people, and sanctifie them to day and to morow, and let them wash their clothes.
19.11: And let them be ready on the third day: for the third day the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai:
19.12: And thou shalt set markes unto the people round about, saying, Take heed to your selves that ye goe not up the mount, nor touch the border of it: whosoever toucheth the mount, shall surely die.
19.13: No hand shall touch it, but he shalbe stoned to death, or striken through with darts: whether it be beast or man, he shall not live: when the horn bloweth long, they shall come up into the mountain.
19.14: Then Moses went down from ye mount unto the people, and sanctified the people, and they washed their clothes.
19.15: And he said unto the people, Be ready on the third day, and come not at your wives.
19.16: And the third day, when it was morning, there was thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the sound of the trumpet exceeding loud, so that all the people, that was in the camp, was afrayde.
19.17: Then Moses brought the people out of the tents to meet with God, and they stood in the nether part of the mount.
19.18: And mount Sinai was all on smoke, because the Lord came down upon it in fire, and the smoke therof ascended, as the smoke of a fornace, and all the mount trembled exceedingly.
19.19: And when the sound of the trumpet blew long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by voyce.
19.20: (For the Lord came down upon mount Sinai on the toppe of the mount) and when the Lord called Moses up into the top of the mount, Moses went up.
19.21: Then the Lord said unto Moses, Go down, charge the people, that they break not their boundes, to go up to the Lord to gaze, least many of them perish.
19.22: And let the Priestes also which come to the Lord be sanctified, least the Lord destroy them.
19.23: And Moses sayde unto the Lord, The people can not come up into the mount Sinai: for thou hast charged us, saying, Set markes on the mountain, and sanctifie it.
19.24: And the Lord sayd unto him, Go, get thee down, and come up, thou, and Aaron with thee: but let not the Priestes and the people break their boundes to come up unto the Lord, least he destroy them.
19.25: So Moses went down unto the people, and told them.

20.1: Then God spake all these wordes, saying,
20.2: I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
20.3: Thou shalt have none other Gods before me.
20.4: Thou shalt make thee no graven image, neither any similitude of things that are in heaven above, neither that are in the earth beneath, nor that are in the waters under the earth.
20.5: Thou shalt not bow down to them, neither serve them: for I am the Lord thy God, a ielous God, visiting the iniquitie of the fathers upon the children, upon the third generation and upon the fourth of them that hate me:
20.6: And shewing mercie unto thousandes to them that love me, and keep my commandemets.
20.7: Thou shalt not take the Name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltles that taketh his Name in vayne.
20.8: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
20.9: Six dayes shalt thou labour, and doe all thy work,
20.10: But the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy sonne, nor thy daughter, thy man servant, nor thy mayde, nor thy beast, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.
20.11: For in six dayes the Lord made the heaven and the earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: therefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day, and hallowed it.
20.12: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy dayes may be prolonged upon the land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
20.16: Thou shalt not bear false witnes against thy neighbour.
