20.17: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbours house, neither shalt thou covet thy neighbours wife, nor his man servant, nor his mayde, nor his oxe, nor his ass, neyther any thing that is thy neighbours.
20.18: And all the people saw the thunders, and the lightnings, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking and when the people saw it they fled and stood afar off,
20.19: And sayde unto Moses, Talk thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God talk with us, lest we die.
20.20: Then Moses sayde unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before you, that ye sinne not.
20.21: So the people stood afarre off, but Moses drew neere unto the darkenes where God was.
20.22: And the Lord sayde unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.
20.23: Ye shall not make therefore with me gods of silver, nor gods of gold: you shall make you none.
20.24: An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and thereon shalt offer thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in all places, where I shall put the remembrance of my Name, I will come unto thee, and bless thee.
20.25: But if thou wilt make mee an altar of stone, thou shalt not buylde it of hewen stones: for if thou lift up thy tool upon them, thou hast polluted them.
20.26: Neither shalt thou goe up by steppes unto mine altar, that thy filthines be not discovered thereon.

21.1: Now these are the lawes, which thou shalt set before them:
21.2: If thou bye an Ebrewe servant, he shall serve six yeres, and in the seventh he shall go out free, for nothing.
21.3: If he came himself alone, he shall goe out himself alone: if hee were married, then his wife shall go out with him.
21.4: If his master have given him a wife, and she hath borne him sonnes or daughters, he wife and her children shalbe her masters, but he shall goe out himself alone.
21.5: But if the servant say thus, I love my master, my wife and my children, I will not goe out free,
21.6: Then his master shall bring him unto the Judges, and set him to the door, or to the post, and his master shall bore his ear through with a nawle, and he shall serve him for ever.
21.7: Likewise if a man sell his daughter to be a servant, she shall not goe out as the men seruantes doe.
21.8: If she please not her master, who hath betrothed her to him self, then shall hee cause to buy her: hee shall have no power to sell her to a strange people, seeing he despised her.
21.9: But if he hath betrothed her unto his sonne, he shall deal with her according to the custom of the daughters.
21.10: If he take him another wife, he shall not diminish her food, her rayment, and recompence of her virginitie.
21.11: And if he do not these three unto her, the shall she go out free, paying no money.
21.12: He that smiteth a man, and he die, shall dye the death.
21.13: And if a man hath not layed wayte, but God hath offered him into his hand, then I wil appoynt thee a place whither he shall flee.
21.14: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
21.15: Also hee that smiteth his father or his mother, shall die the death.
21.16: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, if it be found with him, shall die the death.
21.17: And hee that curseth his father or his mother, shall die the death.
21.18: When men also strive together, and one smite another with a stone, or with the fist, and he die not, but lieth in bed,
21.19: If hee rise again and walk without upon his staff, then shall he that smote him go quite, save onely hee shall bear his charges for his resting, and shall pay for his healing.
21.20: And if a man smite his servant, or his maid with a rod, and he die under his hand, he shalbe surely punished.
21.21: But if he continue a day, or two dayes, hee shall not be punished: for he is his money.
21.22: Also if men strive and hurt a woman with child, so that her child depart from her, and death follow not, hee shall bee surely punished according as the womans husband shall appoynt him, or he shall pay as the Judges determine.
21.23: But if death follow, then thou shalt pay life for life,
21.24: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
21.25: Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
21.26: And if a man smite his servant in the eie, or his maid in the eye, and hath perished it, hee shall let him goe free for his eye.
21.27: Also if he smite out his servants tooth, or his maides tooth, he shall let him goe out free for his tooth.
21.28: If an oxe gore a man or a woman, that he die, the oxe shalbe stoned to death, and his flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the oxe shall goe quite.
21.29: If the oxe were wont to push in times past, and it hath been told his master, and hee hath not kept him, and after he killeth a man or a woman, the oxe shall be stoned, and his owner shall die also.
21.30: If there be set to him a summe of mony, then he shall pay the raunsome of his life, whatsoever shalbe laied upon him.
21.31: Whether he hath gored a sonne or gored a daughter, he shalbe judged after the same maner.
21.32: If the oxe gore a servant or a mayde, hee shall give unto their master thirtie shekels of silver, and the oxe shalbe stoned.
21.33: And when a man shall open a well, or when he shall dig a pit and cover it not, and an oxe or an ass fall therein,
21.34: The owner of the pit shall make it good, and give money to the owners thereof, but the dead beast shalbe his.
21.35: And if a mans oxe hurt his neighbours oxe that he die, then they shall sel the live oxe, and deuide the money thereof, and the dead oxe also they shall deuide.
21.36: Or if it bee knowen that the oxe hath used to push in times past, and his master hath not kept him, he shall pay oxe for oxe, but the dead shall be his own.

22.1: If a man steal an oxe or a sheep, and kill it or sell it, he shall restore five oxen for the oxe, and four sheep for the sheep.
22.2: If a thief bee found breaking up, and be smitten that he dye, no blood shall be shed for him.
22.3: But if it be in the day light, blood shall be shed for him: for he should make full restitution: if he had not wherewith, then should he bee sold for his theft.
22.4: If the theft bee found with him, alive, (whether it be oxe, ass, or sheep) he shall restore the double.
22.5: If a man doe hurt field, or vineyard, and put in his beast to feed in an other mans field, he shall recompence of the best of his own field, and of the best of his own vineyard.
22.6: If fire break out, and catch in ye thornes, and the stackes of corn, or the standing corn, or the field be consumed, he that kindled the fire shall make full restitution.
22.7: If a man deliver his neighbour money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of his house, if the thief be found, he shall pay the double.
22.8: If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shalbe brought unto the Judges to swear, whether he hath put his hand unto his neighbours good, or no.
22.9: In all maner of trespass, whether it bee for oxen, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, or for any maner of lost thing, which an other chalengeth to be his, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges, and whom the Judges condemn, he shall pay the double unto his neighbour.
22.10: If a man deliver unto his neighbour to keep ass, or oxe, or sheep, or any beast, and it die, or be hurt, or taken away by enemies, and no man see it,
22.11: An othe of the Lord shalbe between the twain, that hee hath not put his hand unto his neighbours good, and the owner of it shall take the othe, and he shall not make it good:
22.12: But if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner thereof.
22.13: If it be torn in pieces, he shall bring record, and shall not make that good, which is deuoured.
22.14: And if a man borow ought of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or els die, the owner thereof not being by, he shall surely make it good.
22.15: If the owner thereof bee by, hee shall not make it good: for if it be an hired thing, it came for his hire.
22.16: And if a man entise a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, hee shall endow her, and take her to his wife.
22.17: If her father refuse to give her to him, hee shall pay money, according to ye dowry of virgins.
22.18: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
22.19: Whosoever lieth with a beast, shall dye the death.
22.20: Hee that offereth unto any gods, save unto the Lord onely, shalbe slain.
22.21: Moreover, thou shalt not do iniurie to a stranger, neither oppress him: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.
22.22: Ye shall not trouble any widow, nor fatherless child.
22.23: If thou vex or trouble such, and so he call and cry unto me, I will surely hear his cry.
22.24: Then shall my wrath be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives shall be widowes, and your children fatherless.
22.25: If thou lend money to my people, that is, to the poor with thee, thou shalt not bee as an usurer unto him: yee shall not oppress him with vsurie.
22.26: If thou take thy neighbours rayment to pledge, thou shalt restore it unto him before the sunne go down:
22.27: For that is his covering only, and this is his garment for his skin: wherin shall he sleep? therefore when he crieth unto mee, I will hear him: for I am merciful.
22.28: Thou shalt not rail upon the Judges, neither speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
22.29: Thine abundance and thy licour shalt thou not keep back. The first borne of thy sonnes shalt thou give me.
22.30: Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen and with thy sheep: seven dayes it shall bee with his damme, and the eight day thou shalt give it me.
22.31: Ye shall be an holy people unto me, neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beastes in the field: ye shall cast it to the dogge.

23.1: Thou shalt not receive a false tale, neyther shalt thou put thine hand with the wicked, to be a false witnes.
23.2: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil, neither agree in a controuersie to decline after many and overthrow the trueth.
23.3: Thou shalt not esteem a poor man in his cause.
23.4: If thou meet thine enemies oxe, or his ass going astray, thou shalt bring him to him again.
23.5: If thou see thine enemies ass lying under his burden, wilt thou cease to help him? thou shalt help him up again with it.
23.6: Thou shalt not overthrow the right of thy poor in his sute.
23.7: Thou shalt keep thee far from a false matter, and shalt not slay the innocent and the righteous: for I will not iustifie a wicked man.
23.8: Thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the wordes of the righteous.
23.9: Thou shalt not oppress a stranger: for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing yee were strangers in the land of Egypt.
23.10: Moreover, six yeres thou shalt sow thy land, and gather the fruites thereof,
23.11: But the seventh yeere thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and what they leave, the beastes of the field shall eat. In like maner thou shalt doe with thy vineyard, and with thine olive trees.
23.12: Six dayes thou shalt do thy work, and in the seventh day thou shalt rest, that thine oxe, and thine ass may rest, and the sonne of thy maid and the stranger may be refreshed.
23.13: And ye shall take heed to all things that I have sayde unto you: and ye shall make no mention of the name of other gods, neither shall it be heard out of thy mouth.
23.14: Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the yeere.
23.15: Thou shalt keep the feast of vnleauened bread: thou shalt eat vnleauened bread seue dayes, as I commanded thee, in the season of the moneth of Abib: for in it thou camest out of Egypt: and none shall appear before me emptie:
23.16: The feast also of the harvest of the first fruites of thy labours, which thou hast sowen in the field: and the feast of gathering fruites in the end of the yere, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.
23.17: These three times in the yeere shall all thy men children appear before the Lord Jehovah.
23.18: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread: neyther shall the fatte of my sacrifice remayne until the morning.
23.19: The first of the first fruites of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God: yet shalt thou not seeth a kid in his mothers milk.
23.20: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee to the place which I have prepared.
23.21: Beware of him, and hear his voyce, and provoke him not: for he will not spare your misdeedes, because my name is in him.
23.22: But if thou hearken unto his voyce, and do all that I speak, the I wil be an enemie unto thine enemies, and will afflict them that afflict thee.
23.23: For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I will destroy them.
23.24: Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, neither serve them, nor doe after the workes of them: but utterly overthrow them, and break in pieces their images.
23.25: For ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, and I will take all sickenes away from the middes of thee.
23.26: There shall none cast their fruit nor be baren in thy land: the number of thy dayes will I fulfil.
23.27: I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people among whom thou shalt go: and I will make all thine enemies turn their backes unto thee:
23.28: And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites from thy face.
23.29: I will not cast them out from thy face in one yeere, least the land grow to a wildernes: and the beasts of the field multiplie against thee.
23.30: By litle and litle I will drive them out from thy face, until thou increase, and inherit the land.
23.31: And I will make thy coastes from the red sea unto the sea of the Philistims, and from the desert unto the River: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and thou shalt drive them out from thy face.
23.32: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods:
23.33: Neither shall they dwell in thy land, least they make thee sinne against me: for if thou serve their gods, surely it shall be thy destruction.

24.1: Now hee had said unto Moses, Come up to the Lord, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seuentie of the Elders of Israel, and yee shall worship a far off.
24.2: And Moses himself alone shall come neere to the Lord, but they shall not come neere, neither shall the people goe up with him.
24.3: Afterward Moses came and told the people all the wordes of the Lord, and all the lawes: and all the people answered with one voyce, and said, All the things which the Lord hath said, will we doe.
24.4: And Moses wrote all the wordes of the Lord, and rose up early, and set up an altar under the mountain, and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
24.5: And he sent young men of the children of Israel, which offered burnt offrings of bieues, and sacrificed peace offrings unto the Lord.
24.6: Then Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basens, and half of the blood he sprinckled on the altar.
24.7: After he took the book of the covenant, and read it in the audience of the people: who said, All that the Lord hath said, we will do, and be obedient.
24.8: Then Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold, the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these things.
24.9: Then went up Moses and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seuentie of the Elders of Israel.
24.10: And they saw the God of Israel, and under his feet was as it were a work of a Saphir stone, and as the very heaven when it is clear.
24.11: And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: also they saw God, and did eat and drink.
24.12: And the Lord said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mountain, and be there, and I will give thee tables of stone, and the law and the commandement, which I have written, for to teach them.
24.13: Then Moses rose up, and his minister Joshua, and Moses went up into the mountain of God,
24.14: And said unto the Elders, Tary us here, until we come again unto you: and behold, Aaron, and Hur are with you: whosoever hath any matters, let him come to them.
24.15: Then Moses went up to the mount, and the cloud covered the mountain,
24.16: And the glorie of the Lord abode upon mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six dayes: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the middes of the cloud.
24.17: And the sight of the glorie of the Lord was like consuming fire on the top of the moutaine, in the eyes of the children of Israel.
24.18: And Moses entred into the middes of the cloud, and went up to the mountain: and Moses was in the mount fourtie dayes and fourty nightes.

25.1: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
25.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they receive an offring for me: of every man, whose heart giveth it freely, ye shall take the offring for me.
25.3: And this is the offring which ye shall take of them, gold, and silver, and brass,
25.4: And blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine linen, and goates hear,
25.5: And rammes skinnes coloured red, and the skinnes of badgers, and the wood Shittim,
25.6: Oyle for the light, spices for anoynting oyle, and for the perfume of sweet sauour,
25.7: Onix stones, and stones to be set in the Ephod, and in the brest plate.
25.8: Also they shall make me a Sanctuarie, that I may dwell among them.
25.9: According to all that I shew thee, even so shall ye make the form of the Tabernacle, and the facion of all the instruments thereof.
25.10: They shall make also an Ark of Shittim wood, two cubites and an half long, and a cubit and an half broad, and a cubit and an half hie.
25.11: And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold: within and without shalt thou overlay it, and shalt make upon it a crown of gold round about.
25.12: And thou shalt cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in the four corners thereof: that is, two rings shalbe on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side thereof.
25.13: And thou shalt make barres of Shittim wood, and cover them with gold.
25.14: Then thou shalt put the barres in the rings by the sides of the Ark, to bear the Ark with them.
25.15: The barres shalbe in the rings of the Ark: they shall not be taken away from it.
25.16: So thou shalt put in the Ark the Testimonie which I shall give thee.
25.17: Also thou shalt make a Mercie seat of pure gold, two cubites and an half long, and a cubit and an half broad.
25.18: And thou shalt make two Cherubims of gold: of work beaten out with the hammer shalt thou make the at ye two endes of the Merciseate.
25.19: And the one Cherub shalt thou make at the one end, and the other Cherub at the other end: of the matter of the Mercieseate shall ye make the Cherubims, on the two endes thereof.
25.20: And the Cherubims shall stretch their winges on hie, covering the Mercie seat with their winges, and their faces one to another: to the Mercie seat ward shall the faces of the Cherubims be.
25.21: And thou shalt put the Mercieseate above upon the Ark, and in the Ark thou shalt put the Testimonie, which I will give thee,
25.22: And there I will declare my self unto thee, and from above ye Mercieseate between ye two Cherubims, which are upon ye Ark of ye Testimonie, I wil tel thee al things which I wil give thee in comandement unto ye children of Israel.
25.23: Thou shalt also make a Table of Shittim wood, of two cubites long, and one cubit broad, and a cubit and an half hie:
25.24: And thou shalt cover it with pure gold, and make thereto a crown of gold round about.
25.25: Thou shalt also make unto it a border of four fingers roud about and thou shalt make a golden crown round about the border thereof.
25.26: After, thou shalt make for it four ringes of gold, and shalt put the rings in the four corners that are in the four feet thereof:
25.27: Over against the border shall the rings be for places for barres, to bear the Table.
25.28: And thou shalt make the barres of Shittim wood, and shalt overlay them with gold, that the Table may be borne with them.
25.29: Thou shalt make also dishes for it, and incense cuppes for it, and coverings for it, and goblets, wherewith it shall be covered, even of fine gold shalt thou make them.
25.30: And thou shalt set upon the Table shew bread before me continually.
25.31: Also thou shalt make a Candlestick of pure gold: of work beaten out with the hammer shall the Candlestick be made, his shaft, and his branches, his boules, his knops: and his floures shalbe of the same.
25.32: Six braunches also shall come out of the sides of it: three branches of the Candlestick out of the one side of it, and three branches of the Candlestick out of the other side of it.
25.33: Three boules like unto almondes, one knop and one flour in one braunch: and three boules like almondes in the other branch, one knop and one flour: so throughout the six branches that come out of the Candlestick.
25.34: And in the shaft of the Candlestick shalbe four boules like unto almondes, his knops and his floures.
25.35: And there shalbe a knop under two branches made thereof: and a knop under two branches made thereof: and a knop under two branches made thereof, according to the six branches coming out of the Candlestick.
25.36: Their knops and their branches shall bee thereof. all this shalbe one beaten work of pure gold.
25.37: And thou shalt make the seven lampes thereof: and the lampes thereof shalt thou put thereon, to give light toward that that is before it.
25.38: Also the snuffers and snuffedishes thereof shalbe of pure gold.
25.39: Of a talent of fine gold shalt thou make it with all these instruments.
25.40: Look therefore that thou make them after their facion, that was shewed thee in the mountain.

26.1: Afterward thou shalt make the Tabernacle with tenne curtaines of fine twined linen, and blew silk, and purple, and skarlet: and in them thou shalt make Cherubims of broydered work.
26.2: The length of one curtain shalbe eight and twentie cubites, and the bredth of one curtain, four cubites: every one of the curtaines shall have one measure.
26.3: Five curtaines shalbe coupled one to an other: and the other five curtaines shall be coupled one to another.
26.4: And thou shalt make stringes of blew silk upon the edge of the one curtain, which is in the selvedge of the coupling: and likewise shalt thou make in the edge of the other curtain in the selvedge, in the second coupling.
26.5: Fiftie strings shalt thou make in one curtain, and fiftie stringes shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain, which is in the second coupling: ye stringes shalbe one right against another.
26.6: Thou shalt make also fiftie taches of gold, and couple the curtaines one to another with the taches, and it shalbe one tabernacle.
26.7: Also thou shalt make curtaines of goates hear, to be a covering upon the Tabernacle: thou shalt make them to the number of eleven curtaines.
26.8: The length of a curtain shall be thirtie cubites, and the breadth of a curtain four cubites: the eleven curtaines shalbe of one measure.
26.9: And thou shalt couple five curtaynes by themselves, and the six curtaines by themselves: but thou shalt double the sixt curtain upon the forefront of the covering.
26.10: And thou shalt make fifty stringes in the edge of one curtayne, in the selvedge of the coupling, and fifty stringes in the edge of the other curtain in the second coupling.
26.11: Likewise thou shalt make fifty taches of brass, and fasten them on the strings, and shalt couple the covering together, that it may be one.
26.12: And the remnant that resteth in ye curtaines of the covering, even the half curtain that resteth, shalbe left at the backeside of the Tabernacle,
26.13: That the cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side of that which is left in the legth of the curtaines of ye covering, may remain on either side of the Tabernacle to cover it.
26.14: Moreover, for that covering thou shalt make a covering of rammes skinnes died red, and a covering of badgers skinnes above.
26.15: Also thou shalt make boards for the Tabernacle of Shittim wood to stand up.
26.16: Ten cubites shalbe the length of a board, and a cubit and an half cubit the breadth of one board.
26.17: Two tenons shalbe in one board set in order as the feet of a ladder, one against an other: thus shalt thou make for all the boardes of the Tabernacle.
26.18: And thou shalt make boardes for the Tabernacle, even twenty boardes on the South side, even full South.
26.19: And thou shalt make fourty sockets of silver under the twentie boardes, two sockets under one board for his two tenons, and two sockets under an other board for his two tenons.
26.20: In like maner on the other side of the Tabernacle toward the North side shalbe twentie boardes,
26.21: And their fourtie sockets of silver, two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
26.22: And on the side of the Tabernacle, toward the West shalt thou make six boards.
26.23: Also two boardes shalt thou make in the corners of the Tabernacle in the two sides.
26.24: Also they shalbe ioyned beneath, and likewise they shalbe ioyned above to a ring: thus shall it be for them two: they shalbe for ye two corners.
26.25: So they shalbe eight boardes having sockets of silver, even sixteen sockets, that is, two sockets under one board, and two sockets under an other board.
26.26: The thou shalt make five barres of Shittim wood for the boardes of one side of the Tabernacle,
26.27: And five barres for the boardes of the other side of the Tabernacle: also five barres for the boardes of the side of the Tabernacle toward the Westside.
26.28: And the middle bar shall goe through the middes of the boards, from end to end.
26.29: And thou shalt cover the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold, for places for the barres, and thou shalt cover the barres with gold.
26.30: So thou shalt rear up the Tabernacle, according to the facion thereof, which was shewed thee in the mount.
26.31: Moreover, thou shalt make a vail of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen: thou shalt make it of broydred work with Cherubims.
26.32: And thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of Shittim wood covered with gold, (whose hookes shalbe of gold) stading upon four sockets of silver.
26.33: Afterward thou shalt hang the vail on the hookes, that thou mayest bring in thither, that is (within the vail) the ark of the Testimonie: and the vail shall make you a separation between the Holy place and the most holy place.
26.34: Also thou shalt put ye Mercy seat upon the Ark of the testimonie in the most Holy place.
26.35: And thou shalt set the Table without the vail, and the Candlestick over against the Table on the Southside of the Tabernacle, and thou shalt set the Table on the Northside.
26.36: Also thou shalt make an hanging for the door of ye Tabernacle of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen wrought with needle.
26.37: And thou shalt make for the hanging five pillars of Shittim, and cover them with gold: their heads shalbe of gold, and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.

27.1: Moreover thou shalt make the altar of Shittim wood, five cubites long and five cubites broad (the altar shall be four square) and the height thereof three cubites.
27.2: And thou shalt make it hornes in the four corners thereof: the hornes shalbe of it self, and thou shalt cover it with brass.
27.3: Also thou shalt make his ashpannes for his ashes and his besoms, and his basens, and his flesh-hookes, and his censers: thou shalt make all the instruments thereof of brass.
27.4: And thou shalt make unto it a grate like network of brass: also upon that grate shalt thou make four brasen rings upon the four corners thereof.
27.5: And thou shalt put it under the compass of the altar beneath, that the grate may be in the middes of the altar.
27.6: Also thou shalt make barres for the altar, barres, I say, of Shittim wood, and shalt cover them with brass.
27.7: And the barres thereof shalbe put in the rings, the which barres shalbe upon the two sides of the altar to bear it.
27.8: Thou shalt make the altar holowe between the boardes: as God shewed thee in the mount, so shall they make it.
27.9: Also thou shalt make the court of the Tabernacle in the Southside, even full South: the court shall have curtaines of fine twined linen, of an hundreth cubites long, for one side,
27.10: And it shall have twentie pillars, with their twentie sockets of brass: the heades of the pillars, and their filets shalbe silver.
27.11: Likewise on the Northside in length there shalbe hangings of an hundreth cubites long, and the twentie pillars thereof with their twentie sockets of brass: the heades of the pillars and the filets shalbe silver.
27.12: And the breadth of the court on the Westside shall have curtaines of fiftie cubites, with their ten pillars and their ten sockets.
27.13: And the breadth of the court, Eastward full East shall have fiftie cubites.
27.14: Also hangings of fifteen cubites shalbe on the one side with their three pillars and their three sockets.
27.15: Likewise on the other side shalbe hangings of fifteen cubites, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
27.16: And in the gate of the court shalbe a vail of twentie cubites, of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen wrought with needle, with the four pillars thereof and their four sockets.
27.17: All the pillars of the court shall have filets of silver round about, with their heads of silver, and their sockets of brass.
27.18: The length of the court shalbe an hundreth cubites, and the breadth fiftie at either end, and the height five cubites, and the hangings of fine twined linen, and their sockets of brass.
27.19: Al the vessels of the Tabernacle for al maner service thereof, and all the pinnes thereof, and all the pinnes of the court shalbe brass.
27.20: And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure oyle olive beaten, for the light, that the lampes may alway burn.
27.21: In the Tabernacle of the Congregation without the vail, which is before the Testimony, shall Aaron and his sonnes dress them from evening to morning before the Lord, for a statute for ever unto their generations, to be observed by the children of Israel.

28.1: And cause thou thy brother Aaron to come unto thee and his sonnes with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may serve me in the Priestes office: I mean Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar Aarons sonnes.
28.2: Also thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, glorious and beautiful.
28.3: Therefore thou shalt speak unto al cunning men, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisedome, that they make Aarons garments to consecrate him, that he may serve me in the Priestes office.
28.4: Now these shall be the garments, which they shall make, a brest plate, and an Ephod, and a robe, and a broydred coat, a miter, and a girdle. so these holy garments shall they make for Aaron thy brother, and for his sonnes, that he may serve me in the Priests office.
28.5: Therefore they shall take gold, and blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine linen,
28.6: And they shall make the Ephod of gold, blew silk, and purple, skarlet, and fine twined linen of broydred work.
28.7: The two shoulders thereof shalbe ioyned together by their two edges: so shall it be closed.
28.8: And the embroydred garde of the same Ephod, which shalbe upon him, shall be of the self same work and stuff, even of gold, blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen.
28.9: And thou shalt take two onix stones, and grave upon them the names of the children of Israel:
28.10: Six names of them upon the one stone, and the six names that remain, upon the second stone, according to their generations.
28.11: Thou shalt cause to grave the two stones according to the names of the children of Israel by a grauer of signets, that worketh and graveth in stone, and shalt make them to be set and embossed in gold.
28.12: And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulders of the Ephod, as stones of remebrance of the children of Israel: for Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord upon his two shoulders for a remembrance.
28.13: So thou shalt make bosses of gold,
28.14: And two cheynes of fine gold at the end, of wrethed work shalt thou make them, and shalt fasten the wrethed cheynes upon the bosses.
28.15: Also thou shalt make the brest plate of iudgement with broydred work: like the work of the Ephod shalt thou make it: of gold, blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen shalt thou make it.
28.16: Four square it shall be and double, an hand bredth long and an hand bredth broad.
28.17: Then thou shalt set it full of places for stones, even four rowes of stones: the order shalbe this, a rubie, a topaz, and a carbuncle in the first row.
28.18: And in the second row thou shalt set an emeraude, a saphir, and a diamond.
28.19: And in the third row a turkeis, an achate, and an hematite.
28.20: And in the fourth row a chrysolite, an onix, and a jasper: and they shall be set in gold in their embossements.
28.21: And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, graven as signets, every one after his name, and they shall bee for the twelve tribes.
28.22: Then thou shalt make upon the breast plate two cheines at the endes of wrethen work of pure gold.
28.23: Thou shalt make also upon the brest plate two rings of gold, and put the two rings on the two endes of the brest plate.
28.24: And thou shalt put the two wrethen chaynes of gold in the two rings in the endes of the brest plate.
28.25: And the other two endes of the two wrethen cheines, thou shalt fasten in ye two embossements, and shalt put them upon the shoulders of the Ephod on the foreside of it.
28.26: Also thou shalt make two rings of gold, which thou shalt put in the two other endes of the brest plate, upon the border thereof, toward the inside of the Ephod.
28.27: And two other rings of gold thou shalt make, and put them on the two sides of the Ephod, beneath in the forepart of it over against the coupling of it upon the broydred garde of the Ephod.
28.28: Thus they shall bind the brest plate by his rings unto the rings of the Ephod, with a lace of blew silk, that it may be fast upon the broydred garde of the Ephod, and that the brest plate be not loosed from the Ephod.
28.29: So Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the brest plate of iudgement upon his heart, when he goeth into the holy place, for a remembrance continually before the Lord.
28.30: Also thou shalt put in the brest plate of iudgement the Urim and the Thummim, which shalbe upon Aarons heart, when he goeth in before the Lord: and Aaron shall bear the iudgement of the children of Israel upon his heart before the Lord continually.
28.31: And thou shalt make the robe of the Ephod altogether of blew silk.
28.32: And the hole for his head shalbe in the middes of it, having an edge of woven woorke round about the coller of it: so it shalbe as the coller of an habergeon that it rent not.
28.33: And beneath upon the skirtes thereof thou shalt make pomegranates of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, round about the skirts thereof, and belles of gold between them round about:
28.34: That is, a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate round about upon the skirtes of the robe.
28.35: So it shalbe upon Aaron, when he ministreth, and his sound shalbe heard, when he goeth into the holy place before the Lord, and when he cometh out, and he shall not dye.
28.36: Also thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave thereon, as signets are graven, Holines To The Lord,
28.37: And thou shalt put it on a blew silk lace, and it shalbe upon the miter: even upon the for front of the miter shall it be.
28.38: So it shalbe upon Aarons forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquitie of the offrings, which the children of Israel shall offer in all their holy offrings: and it shall be alwayes upon his forehead, to make them acceptable before the Lord.
28.39: Likewise thou shalt embroyder the fine line coat, and thou shalt make a miter of fine line, but thou shalt make a girdell of needle work.
28.40: Also thou shalt make for Aarons sonnes coates, and thou shalt make the girdels, and bonets shalt thou make them for glorie and comeliness.
28.41: And thou shalt put them upon Aaron thy brother, and on his sonnes with him, and shalt anoint them, and fill their handes, and sanctifie them, that they may minister unto me in the Priestes office.
28.42: Thou shalt also make them linen breeches to cover their priuities: from the loynes unto the thighs shall they reach.
28.43: And they shalbe for Aaron and his sonnes when they come into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, or whe they come unto the altar to minister in the holy place, that they commit not iniquitie, and so die. This shalbe a law for ever unto him and to his seed after him.

29.1: This thing also shalt thou do unto them whe thou consecratest them to be my Priestes, Take a yong calf, and two rams without blemish,
29.2: And vnleauened bread and cakes vnleauened tempered with oyle, and wafers vnleauened anoynted with oyle: (of fine wheat flowre shalt thou make them)
29.3: Then thou shalt put them in one basket, and present them in the basket with the calf and the two rammes,
29.4: And shalt bring Aaron and his sonnes unto the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and wash them with water.
29.5: Also thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the tunicle, and the robe of the Ephod, and the Ephod, and the brest plate, and shalt close them to him with the broidred garde of the Ephod.
29.6: Then thou shalt put the miter upon his head, and shalt put the holy crown upon ye miter.
29.7: And thou shalt take the anoynting oyle, and shalt powre upon his head, and anoynt him.
29.8: And thou shalt bring his sonnes, and put coates upon them,
29.9: And shalt gird them with girdles, both Aaron and his sonnes: and shalt put the bonets on them, and the Priestes office shalbe theirs for a perpetual law: thou shalt also fill the hands of Aaron, and the hands of his sonnes.
29.10: After, thou shalt present the calf before the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and Aaron and his sonnes shall put their handes upon the head of the calf.
29.11: So thou shalt kill the calf before the Lord, at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
29.12: Then thou shalt take of the blood of the calf, and put it upon the hornes of the altar with thy finger, and shalt powre al the rest of the blood at the foot of the altar.
29.13: Also thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inwardes, and the kall, that is on the liver, and the two kidneis, and the fat that is upon them, and shalt burn them upon the altar.
29.14: But the flesh of the calf, and his skin, and his doung shalt thou burn with fire without the host: it is a sinne offring.
29.15: Thou shalt also take one ramme, and Aron and his sonnes shall put their hands upon the head of the ramme.
29.16: Then thou shalt kill the ramme, and take his blood, and sprinkle it round about upon the altar,
29.17: And thou shalt cut the ramme in pieces, and wash the inwards of him and his legges, and shalt put them upon the pieces thereof, and upon his head.
29.18: So thou shalt burn the whole ram upon the altar: for it is a burnt offering unto the Lord for a sweet sauour: it is an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
29.19: And thou shalt take the other ramme, and Aaron and his sonnes shall put their handes upon the head of the ramme.
29.20: Then thou shalt kill the ramme, and take of his blood and put it upon the lappe of Aarons ear, and upon the lappe of the right ear of his sonnes, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and shalt sprinkle the blood upon ye altar roud about.
29.21: And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anoynting oyle, and shalt sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sonnes, and upon the garments of his sonnes with him: so he shall be halowed, and his clothes, and his sonnes, and the garments of his sonnes with him.
29.22: Also thou shalt take of the rammes ye fatte and the rump, even the fat that covereth the inwards, and the kall of the liver, and the two kidneis, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder, (for it is the ramme of consecration)
29.23: And one loaf of bread, and one cake of bread tempered with oyle, and one wafer, out of the basket of the vnleauened bread that is before the Lord.
29.24: And thou shalt put al this in the handes of Aaron, and in the handes of his sonnes, and shalt shake them to and from before the Lord.
29.25: Again, thou shalt receyue them of their handes, and burn them upon the altar besides the burnt offring for a sweet sauour before ye Lord: for this is an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
29.26: Likewise thou shalt take the brest of the ram of the consecration, which is for Aaron, and shalt shake it to and from before the Lord and it shalbe thy part.
29.27: And thou shalt sanctifie the brest of the shaken offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which was shaken to and from, and which was heaved up of the ramme of the consecration, which was for Aaron, and which was for his sonnes.
29.28: And Aaron and his sonnes shall have it by a statute for ever, of the children of Israel: for it is an heave offering, and it shall be an heave offering of the children of Israel, of their peace offerings, even their heave offering to the Lord.
29.29: And the holy garmets, which appertain to Aaron, shall bee his sonnes after him, to bee anoynted therein, and to bee consecrate therein.
29.30: That sonne that shalbe Priest in his stead, shall put them on seven dayes, when he cometh into the Tabernacle of the Congregation to minister in the holy place.
29.31: So thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and seeth his flesh in the holy place.
29.32: And Aaron and his sonnes shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, at the door of ye Tabernacle of ye Congregation.
29.33: So they shall eat these thinges, whereby their atonement was made, to consecrate them, and to sanctifie them: but a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy things.
29.34: Now if ought of the flesh of the consecration, or of the bread remain unto the morning, then thou shalt burn the rest with fire: it shall not be eaten, because it is an holie thing.
29.35: Therefore shalt thou doe thus unto Aaron and unto his sonnes, according to all things, which I have commanded thee: seven dayes shalt thou consecrate them,
29.36: And shalt offer every day a calf for a sinne offring, for reconciliation: and thou shalt cleanse the altar, when thou hast offred upon it for reconciliation, and shalt annoynt it, to sanctifie it.
29.37: Seven dayes shalt thou cleanse the altar, and sanctifie it, so the altar shalbe most holy: and whatsoever toucheth the altar, shalbe holy.
29.38: Now this is that which thou shalt present upon the altar: even two lambes of one yere old, day by day continually.
29.39: The one lamb thou shalt present in the morning, and the other lamb thou shalt present at even.
29.40: And with the one lamb, a tenth part of fine flour mingled with the fourth part of an Hin of beaten oyle, and the fourth part of an Hin of wine, for a drink offring.
29.41: And the other lamb thou shalt present at even: thou shalt doe thereto according to the offring of the morning, and according to the drink offring thereof, to be a burnt offring for a sweet sauour unto, the Lord.
29.42: This shalbe a continual burnt offring in your generations at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation before the Lord, where I wil make appoyntment with you, to speak there unto thee.
29.43: There I will appoynt with the children of Israel, and the place shall bee sanctified by my glorie.
29.44: And I will sanctifie the Tabernacle of the Congregation and the altar: I will sanctifie also Aaron and his sonnes to be my Priests,
29.45: And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will bee their God.
29.46: Then shall they know that I am ye Lord their God, that brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I might dwell among them: I am the Lord their God.

30.1: Furthermore thou shalt make an altar for sweet perfume, of Shittim wood thou shalt make it.
30.2: The length therof a cubit and the breadth thereof a cubit (it shalbe four square) and the height thereof two cubites: the hornes thereof shalbe of the same,
30.3: And thou shalt overlay it with fine gold, both the toppe therof and the sides thereof round about, and his hornes: also thou shalt make unto it a crown of gold round about.
30.4: Besides this thou shalt make under this crown two golden rings on either side: even on every side shalt thou make them, that they may be as places for the barres to bear it withal.
30.5: The which barres thou shalt make of Shittim wood, and shalt cover them with gold.
30.6: After thou shalt set it before the vail, that is neere the Ark of Testimonie, before the Merciseate that is upon the Testimonie, where I will appoynt with thee.
30.7: And Aaron shall burn thereon sweet incense every morning: when hee dresseth the lampes thereof, shall he burn it.
30.8: Likewise at eve, when Aaron setteth up the lampes thereof, he shall burn incense: this perfume shalbe perpetually before ye Lord, throughout your generations.
30.9: Ye shall offer no strange incense thereon, nor burnt sacrifice, nor offring, neither powre any drink offring thereon.
30.10: And Aaron shall make reconciliation upon the hornes of it once in a yere with the blood of the sinne offring in the day of reconciliation: once in the yeere shall hee make reconciliation upon it throughout your generations: this is most holy unto the Lord.
30.11: Afterward the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
30.12: When thou takest the summe of the children of Israel after their nomber, then they shall give every man a redemption of his life unto the Lord, when thou tellest them, that there bee no plague among the when thou countest them.
30.13: This shall every man give, that goeth into the nomber, half a shekel, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie: (a shekel is twentie gerahs) the half shekel shalbe an offring to the Lord.
30.14: All that are nombred from twentie yeere old and above, shall give an offring to the Lord.
30.15: The rich shall not pass, and the poor shall not diminish from half a shekel, when ye shall give an offring unto the Lord, for the redemption of your lives.
30.16: So thou shalt take the money of the redemption of the children of Israel, and shalt put it unto the use of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, that it may be a memorial unto the children of Israel before the Lord for the redemption of your lives.
30.17: Also the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
30.18: Thou shalt also make a laver of brass, and his foot of brass to wash, and shalt put it between the Tabernacle of the Congregation and the Altar, and shalt put water therein.
30.19: For Aaron and his sonnes shall wash their hands and their feet thereat.
30.20: When they go into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, or when they goe unto the Altar to minister and to make the perfume of ye burnt offring to the Lord, they shall wash themselves with water, lest they die.
30.21: So they shall wash their handes and their feet that they die not: and this shall be to them an ordinance for ever, both unto him and to his seed throughout their generations.
30.22: Also the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
30.23: Take thou also unto thee, principal spices of the most pure myrrh five hundreth shekels, of sweet cinamon half so much, that is, two hundreth and fiftie, and of sweet calamus, two hundreth, and fiftie:
30.24: Also of cassia five hundreth, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, and of oyle olive an Hin.
30.25: So thou shalt make of it the oyle of holie oyntment, even a most precious oyntment after the art of the Apothecarie: this shalbe the oyle of holy oyntment.
30.26: And thou shalt anoynt the Tabernacle of the Congregation therewith, and the Ark of the Testimonie:
30.27: Also the Table, and al the instruments thereof, and the Candlestick, with all the instruments thereof, and the altar of incense:
30.28: Also the Altar of burnt offring with al his instruments, and the laver and his foot.
30.29: So thou shalt sanctifie them, and they shalbe most holy: all that shall touch them, shalbe holy.
30.30: Thou shalt also anoint Aaron and his sonnes, and shalt consecrate them, that they may minister unto me in the Priests office.
30.31: Moreover thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, This shalbe an holy oynting oyle unto me, throughout your generations.
30.32: None shall anoynt, mans flesh therewith, neither shall ye make any composition like unto it: for it is holy, and shalbe holy unto you.
30.33: Whosoever shall make the like oyntment, or whosoever shall put any of it upon a stranger, even he shalbe cut off from his people.
30.34: And the Lord sayd unto Moses, Take unto thee these spices, pure myrrh and clear gumme and galbanum, these odours with pure frankincense, of eche like weight:
30.35: Then thou shalt make of them perfume composed after the art of the apothecarie, mingled together, pure and holy.
30.36: And thou shalt beat it to pouder, and shalt put of it before the Ark of the Testimonie in the Tabernacle of ye Cogregatio, where I wil make appointmet with thee: it shalbe unto you most holy.
30.37: And ye shall not make unto you any composition like this perfume, which thou shalt make: it shalbe unto thee holy for the Lord.
30.38: Whosoever shall make like unto that to smell thereto, even he shalbe cut off from his people.

31.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
31.2: Behold, I have called by name, Bezaleel the sonne of Uri, the sonne of Hur of the tribe of Judah,
31.3: Whom I have filled with the Spirit of God, in wisedome, and in understanding and in knowledge and in all workmanship:
31.4: To find out curious workes to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
31.5: Also in the art to set stones, and to carue in timber, and to work in all maner of workmaship.
31.6: And behold, I have ioyned with him Aholiab the sonne of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted, have I put wisdom to make all that I have commanded thee:
31.7: That is, the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and the Ark of the Testimonie, and the Merciseate that shalbe thereupon, with all instruments of the Tabernacle:
31.8: Also the Table and the instruments thereof, and the pure Candlestick with all his instruments, and the Altar of perfume:
31.9: Likewise the Altar of burnt offring with al his instruments, and the Laver with his foot:
31.10: Also the garments of the ministration, and ye holy garments for Aaron ye Priest, and the garmets of his sonnes, to minister in the Priestes office,
31.11: And the anoynting oyle, and sweet perfume for the Sanctuarie: according to all that I have commanded thee, shall they do.
31.12: Afterward the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
31.13: Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, and say, Notwithstanding keep yee my Sabbaths: for it is a sign between me and you in your generations, that ye may know that I the Lord do sanctifie you.
31.14: Ye shall therefore keep the Sabbath: for it is holy unto you: he that defileth it, shall die the death: therefore whosoever worketh therin, the same person shalbe even cut off from among his people.
31.15: Six dayes shall men work, but in the seventh day is the Sabbath of the holy rest to the Lord: whosoever doeth any work in the Sabbath day, shall dye the death.
31.16: Wherfore the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, that they may observe the rest throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant.
31.17: It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six dayes the Lord made the heaven and the earth, and in the seventh day he ceased, and rested.
31.18: Thus (when the Lord had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai) he gave him two Tables of the Testimonie, even tables of stone, written with the finger of God.

32.1: But when the people saw, that Moses taryed long or he came down from the mountain, the people gathered themselves together against Aaron, and sayde unto him, Up, make us gods to goe before us: for of this Moses (the man that brought us out of the land of Egypt) we know not what is become of him.
32.2: And Aaron said unto them, Pluck off the golden earings, which are in the eares of your wives, of your sonnes, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
32.3: Then all ye people pluckt from them selves the golden earings, which were in their eares, and they brought them unto Aaron.
32.4: Who received them at their handes, and facioned it with the graving tool, and made of it a molte calf: then they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee out of ye lad of Egypt
32.5: When Aaron saw that, he made an Altar before it: and Aaron proclaimed, saying, To morow shalbe the holy day of the Lord.
32.6: So they rose up the next day in the morning, and offred burnt offerings, and brought peace offrings: also the people sat them down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
32.7: Then the Lord said unto Moses, Go, get thee down: for thy people which thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, hath corrupted their wayes.
32.8: They are soon turned out of the way, which I commanded them: for they have made them a molten calf and have worshipped it, and have offered thereto, saying, These be thy gods, O Israel, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
32.9: Again the Lord said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff necked people.
32.10: Now therefore let mee alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, for I wil consume the: but I wil make of thee a mighty people.
32.11: But Moses praied unto the Lord his God, and said, O Lord, why doeth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, with great power and with a mightie hand?
32.12: Wherefore shall the Egyptians speak, and say, He hath brought them out maliciously for to slay them in the mountaines, and to consume them from the earth? turn from thy fearce wrath, and change thy mind from this evil toward thy people.
32.13: Remember Abraham, Izhak, and Israel thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self, and saydest unto them, I wil multiply your seed, as the starres of the heaven, and all this land, that I have spoken of, wil I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.
32.14: Then the Lord changed his mind from the evil, which he threatned to do unto his people.
32.15: So Moses returned and went down from the mountain with the two Tables of the Testimonie in his hand: the Tables were written on both their sides, even on the one side and on the other were they written.
32.16: And these Tables were the work of God, and this writing was the writing of God graven in the Tables.
32.17: And when Joshua heard the noyse of the people, as they shouted, he said unto Moses, There is a noyse of war in the host.
32.18: Who answered, It is not the noyse of them that have the victorie, nor the noyse of them that are overcome: but I do hear ye noyse of singing.
32.19: Now, as soon as he came neere unto the host, he saw the calf and the dancing: so Moses wrath waxed hot, and he cast the Tables out of his handes, and brake them in pieces beneath the mountain.
32.20: After, he took the calf, which they had made, and burned it in the fire, and ground it unto powder, and strowed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.
32.21: Also Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sinne upon them?
32.22: Then Aaron answered, Let not the wrath of my Lord wax fearce: Thou knowest this people, that they are even set on mischief.
32.23: And they sayde unto me, Make us gods to go before us: for we know not what is become of this Moses (the man that brought us out of the land of Egypt.)
32.24: Then I sayde to them, Ye that have gold, pluck it off: and they brought it me, and I did cast it into the fire, and thereof came this calf.
32.25: Moses therefore saw that the people were naked (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies)
32.26: And Moses stood in ye gate of the camp, and sayde, Who pertaineth to the Lord? let him come to mee. And all the sonnes of Levi gathered themselves unto him.
32.27: Then he said unto them, Thus sayth ye Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side: go to and from, from gate to gate, through the host, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
32.28: So the children of Levi did as Moses had commanded: and there fel of the people the same day about three thousand men.
32.29: (For Moses had said, Cosecrate your hands unto the Lord this day, even every man upon his sonne, and upon his brother, that there may be given you a blessing this day)
32.30: And when the morning came, Moses sayde unto the people, Yee have committed a grieuous crime: but now I wil goe up to the Lord, if I may pacifie him for your sinne.
32.31: Moses therefore went again unto ye Lord, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sinne, and have made them gods of gold.
32.32: Therefore now if thou pardon their sinne, thy mercy shall appear: but if thou wilt not, I pray thee, rase me out of thy book, which thou hast written.
32.33: Then the Lord sayd to Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, I will put out of my book.
32.34: Go now therefore, bring the people unto the place which I commanded thee: behold, mine Angel shall goe before thee, but yet in the day of my visitation I wil visit their sinne upon them.
32.35: So the Lord plagued the people, because they caused Aaron to make ye calf which he made.

33.1: Afterward the Lord sayd unto Moses, Depart, goe up from hence, thou, and the people (which thou hast brought up out of land of Egypt) unto the land which I sware unto Abraham, to Izhak and to Iaakob, saying, Unto thy seed will I give it.
33.2: And I will send an Angel before thee and will cast out the Canaanites, the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites:
33.3: To a land, I say, that floweth with milk and hony: for I will not goe up with thee, because thou art a stiff necked people, least I consume thee in the way.
33.4: And when the people heard this evil tydings, they sorowed, and no man put on his best rayment.
33.5: (For the Lord had said to Moses, Say unto the children of Israel, Ye are a stiff necked people, I wil come suddenly upon thee, and consume thee: therefore now put thy costly rayment from thee, that I may know what to do unto thee)
33.6: So the children of Israel layed their good raiment from them, after Moses came down from the mount Horeb.
33.7: Then Moses took his tabernacle, and pitched it without the host far off from the host, and called it Ohel-moed. And whe any did seek to the Lord, he went out unto the Tabernacle of the Congregation, which was without the host.
33.8: And when Moses went out unto the Tabernacle, all the people rose up, and stood every man at his tent door, and looked after Moses, until he was gone into the Tabernacle.
33.9: And assoone as Moses was entred into the Tabernacle, the cloudie pillar descended and stood at the door of the Tabernacle, and the Lord talked with Moses.
33.10: Now when all the people saw the cloudie pillar stand at the Tabernacle door, all the people rose up, and worshipped every man in his tent door.
33.11: And the Lord spake unto Moses, face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. After he turned again into the host, but his servant Joshua the sonne of Nun a yong man, departed not out of the Tabernacle.
33.12: Then Moses sayde unto the Lord, See, thou sayest unto me, Lead this people forth, and thou hast not shewed me whom thou wilt send with mee: thou hast sayde moreover, I know thee by name, and thou hast also found grace in my sight.
33.13: Now therefore, I pray thee, if I have found fauour in thy sight, shew mee now thy way, that I may know thee, and that I may find grace in thy sight: consider also that this nation is thy people.
33.14: And he answered, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.
33.15: Then he sayd unto him, If thy presence go not with us, cary us not hence.
33.16: And wherein now shall it be knowen, that I and thy people have found fauour in thy sight? shall it not be when thou goest with us? so I, and thy people shall have preeminence before all the people that are upon the earth.
33.17: And the Lord sayde unto Moses, I will doe this also that thou hast said: for thou hast found grace in my sight, and I know thee by name.
33.18: Again he sayde, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.
33.19: And he answered, I wil make all my good go before thee, and I wil proclaim the Name of the Lord before thee: for I will shew mercy to whom I will shew mercy, and will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
33.20: Furthermore he sayde, Thou canst not see my face, for there shall no man see me, and live.
33.21: Also the Lord sayd, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon the rock:
33.22: And while my glory passeth by, I will put thee in a cleft of the rock, and will cover thee with mine hand whiles I pass by.
33.23: After I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.

34.1: And the Lord said unto Moses, Hew thee two Tables of stone, like unto the first, and I will write upon the Tables the wordes that were in the first Tables, which thou brakest in pieces.
34.2: And be ready in ye morning, that thou mayest come up earely unto the mount of Sinai, and wait there for me in the top of the mount.
34.3: But let no man come up with thee, neither let any man be seen throughout all the mount, neyther let the sheep nor cattell feed before this mount.
34.4: Then Moses hewed two Tables of stone like unto the first, and rose up earely in the morning, and went up unto the mount of Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, and took in his hand two Tables of stone.
34.5: And the Lord descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the Lord.
34.6: So the Lord passed before his face, and cried, The Lord, the Lord, strong, merciful, and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in goodness and trueth,
34.7: Reseruing mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquitie, and transgression and sinne, and not making the wicked innocent, visiting the iniquitie of the fathers upon ye children, and upon childrens children, unto the third and fourth generation.
34.8: Then Moses made haste and bowed him self to the earth, and worshipped,
34.9: And sayde, O Lord, I pray thee, If I have found grace in thy sight, that the Lord would now goe with us ( for it is a stiff necked people) and pardon our iniquitie and our sinne, and take us for thine inheritance.
34.10: And he answered, Behold, I will make a covenant before all thy people, and will do marueiles, such as have not been done in all the world, neyther in all nations: and all the people among whom thou art, shall see the work of the Lord: for it is a terrible thing that I will do with thee.
34.11: Keep diligently that which I command thee this day: Behold, I will cast out before thee the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
34.12: Take heed to thy self, that thou make no compact with ye inhabitantes of the land whither thou goest, least they be the cause of ruin among you:
34.13: But yee shall overthrow their altars, and break their images in pieces, and cut down their groves,
34.14: (For thou shalt bow down to none other god, because the Lord, whose Name is Ielous, is a ielous God)
34.15: Lest thou make a compact with the inhabitantes of the land, and when they goe a whoring after their gods, and doe sacrifice unto their gods, some man call thee, and thou eat of his sacrifice:
34.16: And least thou take of their daughters unto thy sonnes, and their daughters goe a whoring after their gods, and make thy sonnes goe a whoring after their gods.
34.17: Thou shalt make thee no gods of metall.
34.18: The feast of vnleauened bread shalt thou keep: seven dayes shalt thou eat vnleauened bread, as I commanded thee, in ye time of the moneth of Abib: for in the moneth of Abib thou camest out of Egypt.
34.19: Every male, that first openeth the womb, shalbe mine: also all the first borne of thy flock shalbe rekoned mine, both of beeves and sheep.
34.20: But ye first of ye ass thou shalt bie out with a lamb: and if thou redeem him not, then thou shalt break his neck: all the first borne of thy sonnes shalt thou redeem, and none shall appear before me emptie.
34.21: Six dayes shalt thou work, and in the seventh day thou shalt rest: both in earing time, and in the harvest thou shalt rest.
34.22: Thou shalt also observe the feast of weekes in the time of ye first fruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of gathering fruites in the end of the yere.
34.23: Thrise in a yere shall all your men children appear before the Lord Jehovah God of Israel.
34.24: For I wil cast out the nations before thee, and enlarge thy coasts, so that no man shall desire thy land, whe thou shalt come up to appear before the Lord thy God thrise in the yeere.
34.25: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven, neither shall ought of the sacrifice of the feast of Passeouer be left unto the morning.
34.26: The first ripe fruites of thy land thou shalt bring unto the house of the Lord thy God: yet shalt thou not seethe a kid in his mothers milk.
34.27: And the Lord said unto Moses, Write thou these words: for after the tenour of these words I have made a covenant with thee and with Israel.
34.28: So hee was there with the Lord fourtie dayes and fourtie nights, and did neither eat bread nor drink water: and hee wrote in the Tables the wordes of the covenant, even the tenne commandements.
34.29: So when Moses came down from mount Sinai, the two Tables of the Testimonie were in Moses hand, as hee descended from the mount: (now Moses wist not that the skinne of his face shone bright, after that God had talked with him.
34.30: And Aaron and all the children of Israel looked upon Moses, and behold, the skin of his face shone bright, and they were afraid to come neere him)
34.31: But Moses called them: and Aaron and all the chief of the congregation returned unto him: and Moses talked with them.
34.32: And afterward all the children of Israel came neere, and he charged them with al that the Lord had said unto him in mount Sinai.
34.33: So Moses made an end of comuning with them, and had put a covering upon his face.
34.34: But, when Moses came before the Lord to speak with him, he took off the covering until he came out: then he came out, and spake unto the children of Israel that which he was commanded.
34.35: And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, how the skin of Moses face shone bright: therefore Moses put the covering upon his face, until he went to speak with God.

35.1: Then Moses assembled all the Congregation of the children of Israel, and sayd unto them, These are the wordes which the Lord hath commanded, that ye should do them:
35.2: Six dayes thou shalt work, but the seventh day shall bee unto you the holy Sabbath of rest unto the Lord: whosoever doth any work therein, shall die.
35.3: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout all your habitations upon the Sabbath day.
35.4: Again, Moses spake unto all the Congregation of the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing which the Lord commandeth, saying,
35.5: Take from among you an offering unto the Lord: whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring this offring to the Lord, namely gold, and silver, and brass:
35.6: Also blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine linen, and goates hear,
35.7: And rams skins died red, and badgers skins with Shittim wood:
35.8: Also oyle for light, and spices for the anointing oyle, and for the sweet incense,
35.9: And onix stones, and stones to be set in the Ephod, and in the brest plate.
35.10: And all the wise hearted among you, shall come and make all that the Lord hath commanded:
35.11: That is, the Tabernacle, that pavilion thereof, and his covering, and his taches and his boards, his barres, his pillars and his sockets,
35.12: The Ark, and the barres thereof ye Merci-seat, and the vail that covereth it,
35.13: The Table, and the barres of it, and all the instruments thereof, and the shew bread:
35.14: Also the Candlestick of light and his instruments, and his lampes with the oyle for the light:
35.15: Likewise the Altar of perfume and his barres, and the anoynting oyle, and the sweet incense, and the vail of the door at the entring in of the Tabernacle,
35.16: The Altar of burnt offering with his brasen grate, his barres and all his instruments, the Laver and his foot,
35.17: The hangings of the court, his pillars and his sockets, and the vail of the gate of the court,
35.18: The pinnes of the Tabernacle, and the pinnes of the court with their cordes,
35.19: The ministring garments to minister in the holy place, and the holy garments for Aaron the Priest, and the garmentes of his sonnes, that they may minister in the Priests office.
35.20: Then all the Congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.
35.21: And every one, whose heart encouraged him, and every one, whose spirit made him willing, came and brought an offring to the Lord, for the work of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and for all his uses, and for the holy garments.
35.22: Both men and women, as many as were free hearted, came and brought taches and earings, and rings, and bracelets, all were jewels of gold: and every one that offered an offring of gold unto the Lord:
35.23: Every man also, which had blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine linen, and goates hear, and rammes skinnes died red, and badgers skins, brought them.
35.24: All that offered an oblation of silver and of brass, brought the offring unto the Lord: and every one, that had Shittim wood for any maner work of the ministration, brought it.
35.25: And all the women that were wise hearted, did spin with their hands, and brought ye spun work, even the blew silk, and the purple, the skarlet, and the fine linen.
35.26: Likewise al the women, whose hearts were moved with knowledge, spun goates hear.
35.27: And ye rulers brought onix stones, and stones to be set in the Ephod, and in the brest plate:
35.28: Also spice, and oyle for light, and for the anoynting oyle, and for the sweet perfume.
35.29: Every man and woman of the children of Israel, whose hearts moved the willingly to bring for all the work which the Lord had commanded the to make by the hand of Moses, brought a free offring to the Lord.
35.30: Then Moses sayde unto the children of Israel, Behold, the Lord hath called by name Bezaleel the sonne of Uri, the sonne of Hur of the tribe of Judah,
35.31: And hath filled him with an excellent spirit of wisdom, of understanding, and of knowledge, and in all maner work,
35.32: To find out curious workes, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
35.33: And in graving stones to set them, and in karuing of wood, even to make any maner of fine work.
35.34: And he hath put in his heart that hee may teach other: both hee, and Aholiab the sonne of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan:
35.35: Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart to work all maner of cunning and broidred, and needle work: in blew silk, and in purple, in skarlet, and in fine linen and weauing, even to do all maner of work and subtil inventions.

36.1: Then wrought Bezaleel, and Aholiab, and all cunning men, to whom the Lord gave wisedome, and understanding, to know how to work all maner work for the service of the Sanctuarie, according to all that the Lord had commanded.
36.2: For Moses had called Bezaleel, and Aholiab, and all the wise hearted men, in whose heartes the Lord had given wisedome, even as many as their hearts encouraged to come unto that work to work it.
36.3: And they received of Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the Sanctuary, to make it: also they brought still unto him free giftes every morning.
36.4: So all the wise men, that wrought all the holy work, came every man from his work which they wrought,
36.5: And spake to Moses, saying, The people bring too much, and more then ynough for the use of the work, which the Lord hath commanded to be made.
36.6: Then Moses gave a commandement, and they caused it to be proclaymed throughout the host, saying, Let neither man nor woman prepare any more work for the oblation of the Sanctuarie. So the people were stayed from offring.
36.7: For the stuff they had, was sufficient for all the work to make it, and too much.
36.8: All the cunning men therefore among the workemen, made for the Tabernacle ten curtaines of fine twined linen, and of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet: Cherubims of broydred work made they upon them.
36.9: The length of one curtain was twentie and eight cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubites: and the curtaines were all of one cis.
36.10: And he coupled five curtaines together, and other five coupled he together.
36.11: And he made strings of blew silk by the edge of one curtain, in the selvedge of the coupling: likewise he made on the side of the other curtain in the selvedge in the second coupling.
36.12: Fiftie strings made he in the one curtain, and fiftie strings made he in the edge of the other curtain, which was in the second coupling: the strings were set one against another.
36.13: After, he made fiftie taches of gold, and coupled the curtaines one to another with the taches: so was it one Tabernacle.
36.14: Also he made curtaines of goates hear for the covering upon the Tabernacle: he made them to the nomber of eleven curtaines.
36.15: The length of one curtain had thirtie cubites, and the bredth of one curtain four cubites: the eleven curtaines were of one cis.
36.16: And hee coupled five curtaines by themselves, and six curtaines by themselves:
36.17: Also he made fiftie strings upon the edge of one curtain in the selvedge in the coupling, and fiftie strings made hee upon the edge of the other curtain in the second coupling.
36.18: He made also fiftie taches of brass to couple the covering that it might be one.
36.19: And he made a covering upon the pavilion of rams skinnes dyed red, and a covering of badgers skinnes above.
36.20: Likewise he made the boards for the Tabernacle, of Shittim wood to stand up.
36.21: The length of a board was ten cubites, and the bredth of one board was a cubit, and an half.
36.22: One board had two tenons, set in order as the feet of a ladder, one against another: thus made he for all the boardes of the Tabernacle.
36.23: So he made twentie boardes for the South side of the Tabernacle, even full South.
36.24: And fourtie sockets of silver made he under the twentie boardes, two sockets under one board for his two tenons, and two sockets under another board for his two tenons.
36.25: Also for the other side of the Tabernacle toward the North, he made twentie boards,
36.26: And their fourtie sockets of silver, two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
36.27: Likewise toward the Westside of the Tabernacle he made six boardes.
36.28: And two boardes made he in the corners of the Tabernacle, for either side,
36.29: And they were ioyned beneath, and likewise were made sure above with a ring: thus he did to both in both corners.
36.30: So there were eight boards and their sixteen sockets of silver, under every board two sockets.
36.31: After, he made barres of Shittim wood, five for the boards in ye one side of ye Tabernacle,
36.32: And five barres for the boardes in the other side of the Tabernacle, and five barres for the boards of the Tabernacle on the side toward the West.
36.33: And he made the middest bar to shoot through the boards, from the one end to ye other.
36.34: He ouerlayd also the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold for places for the barres, and covered the barres with gold.
36.35: Moreover he made a vail of blew silk, and purple, and of skarlet, and of fine twined linen: with Cherubims of broydred work made he it:
36.36: And made thereunto four pillars of Shittim, and ouerlayd them with gold: whose hookes were also of gold, and hee cast for them four sockets of silver.
36.37: And he made an hanging for the Tabernacle door, of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen, and needle work,
36.38: And the five pillars of it with their hookes, and ouerlayde their chapiters and their filets with gold, but their five sockets were of brass.

37.1: After this, Bezaleel made the Ark of Shittim wood, two cubites and an half long and a cubit and an half broad, and a cubit and an half hie:
37.2: And ouerlayde it with fine gold within and without, and made a crown of gold to it round about,
37.3: And cast for it four rings of gold for the four corners of it: that is, two rings for the one side of it, and two rings for the other side thereof.
37.4: Also he made barres of Shittim wood, and covered them with gold,
37.5: And put the barres in the rings by the sides of the Ark, to bear the Ark.
37.6: And he made the Merciseate of pure gold: two cubites and an half was the length thereof, and one cubit and an half the breadth thereof.
37.7: And he made two Cherubims of gold, upon the two endes of the Merciseate: even of work beaten with the hammer made he them.
37.8: One Cherub on the one end, and another Cherub on the other end: of the Merciseate made he the Cherubims, at ye two endes thereof.
37.9: And the Cherubims spread out their wings on hie, and covered the Merciseat with their wings, and their faces were one towards another: toward the Merciseat were the faces of the Cherubims.
37.10: Also he made ye Table of Shittim wood: two cubites was the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and an half the height of it.
37.11: And hee ouerlayde it with fine gold, and made thereto a crown of gold round about.
37.12: Also he made thereto a border of an hand breadth round about, and made upon the border a crown of gold round about.
37.13: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that were in the four feet thereof.
37.14: Against the border were the rings, as places for the barres to bear the Table.
37.15: And he made the barres of Shittim wood, and covered them with gold to bear the Table.
37.16: Also he made the instruments for the Table of pure gold: dishes for it, and incense cuppes for it, and goblets for it, and coverings for it, wherewith it should be covered.
37.17: Likewise he made the Candlestick of pure gold: of work beaten out with the hammer made he the Candlestick: and his shaft, and his branch, his bolles, his knops, and his floures were of one piece.
37.18: And six branches came out of the sides thereof: three branches of the Candlestick out of the one side of it, and three branches of the Candlestick out of the other side of it.
