37.19: In one branch three bolles made like almondes, a knop and a flour: and in another branch three bolles made like almondes, a knop and a flour: and so throughout the six branches that proceeded out of the Candlestick.
37.20: And upon the Candlestick were four bolles after the facion of almondes, the knoppes thereof and the floures thereof:
37.21: That is, under every two branches a knop made thereof, and a knop under the second branch thereof, and a knop under the third branch thereof, according to the six branches coming out of it.
37.22: Their knops and their branches were of the same: it was all one beaten work of pure gold.
37.23: And he made for it seven lampes with the snuffers, and snufdishes thereof of pure gold.
37.24: Of a talent of pure gold made he it with all the instruments thereof.
37.25: Furthermore he made the perfume altar of Shittim wood: the length of it was a cubit, and the breadth of it a cubit (it was square) and two cubites hie, and the hornes thereof were of ye same.
37.26: And he covered it with pure gold, both the top and the sides thereof round about, and the hornes of it, and made unto it a crown of gold round about.
37.27: And he made two rings of gold for it, under the crown thereof in the two corners of the two sides thereof, to put barres in for to bear it therewith.
37.28: Also he made the barres of Shittim wood, and ouerlayde them with gold.
37.29: And he made the holy anointing oyle, and the sweet pure incense after ye apothecaries art.

38.1: Also he made the altar of the burnt offering of Shittim wood: five cubites was the length therof, and five cubites the breadth thereof: it was square and three cubites hie.
38.2: And hee made unto it hornes in the four corners thereof: the hornes thereof were of the same, and he ouerlayd it with brass.
38.3: Also he made al the instruments of the altar: the ashpans, and the besoms, and the basins, the fleshhookes, and the censers: all the instruments thereof made he of brass.
38.4: Moreover he made a brasen grate wrought like a net to the Altar, under the compass of it beneath in the middes of it,
38.5: And cast four rings of brass for the four endes of the grate to put barres in.
38.6: And he made the barres of Shittim wood, and covered them with brass.
38.7: The which barres he put into the rings on the sides of the altar to bear it withal, and made it hollow within the boardes.
38.8: Also he made the Laver of brass, and the foot of it of brass of the glasses of the women that did assemble and came together at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
38.9: Finally he made the court on the South side full South: the hangings of the court were of fine twined linen, having an hundreth cubites.
38.10: Their pillars were twentie, and their brasen sockets twentie: the hookes of the pillars, and their filets were of silver.
38.11: And on the Northside the hanginges were an hundreth cubites: their pillars twentie, and their sockets of brass twentie, the hookes of the pillars and their filets of silver.
38.12: On the Westside also were hangings of fiftie cubites, their ten pillars with their ten sockets: the hookes of the pillars and their filets of silver.
38.13: And toward ye Eastside, full East were hangings of fiftie cubites.
38.14: The hangings of the one side were fifteen cubites, their three pillars, and their three sockets:
38.15: And of the other side of the court gate on both sides were hangings of fifteen cubites, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
38.16: All the hangings of the court round about were of fine twined linen:
38.17: But the sockets of ye pillars were of brass: the hookes of the pillars and their filets of silver, and the covering of their chapiters of silver: and all the pillars of the court were hooped about with silver.
38.18: He made also the hanging of the gate of the court of needle work, blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen even twentie cubites long, and five cubites in height and bredth, like the hangings of the court.
38.19: And their pillars were four with their four sockets of brass: their hookes of silver, and the covering of their chapiters, and their filets of silver.
38.20: But all the pins of the Tabernacle and of the court round about were of brass.
38.21: These are the parts of the Tabernacle, I mean, of the Tabernacle of the Testimonie, which was appovnted by the commandement of Moses for the office of the Levites by the hand of Ithamar sonne to Aaron the Priest.
38.22: So Bezaleel the sonne of Uri the sonne of Hur of the tribe of Judah, made all that the Lord commanded Moses.
38.23: And with him Aholiab sonne of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, a cunning workeman and an embroiderer and a worker of needle work in blew silk, and in purple, and in skarlet, and in fine linen.
38.24: All ye gold that was occupied in all ye work wrought for the holy place (which was the gold of the offring) was nine and twentie talents, and seven hundreth and thirtie shekels, according to the shekel of the Sanctuarie.
38.25: But the silver of them that were numbred in the Congregation, was an hundreth talents, and a thousand seven hundreth seuentie and five shekels, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie.
38.26: A portion for a man, that is, half a shekel after ye shekel of the Sanctuarie, for all them that were numbred from twentie yeere old and above, among six hundreth thousand, and three thousand, and five hundreth and fiftie men.
38.27: Moreover there were an hundreth talentes of silver, to cast ye sockets of ye Sanctuary, and the sockets of the vail: an hundreth sockets of an hundreth talents, a talent for a socket.
38.28: But he made the hookes for the pillars of a thousand seven hundreth and seuentie and five shekels, and ouerlayde their chapiters, and made filets about them.
38.29: Also the brass of the offering was seuentie talents, and two thousand, and four hundreth shekels.
38.30: Whereof he made the sockets to the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and the brasen altar, and the brasen grate which was for it, with all the instruments of the Altar,
38.31: And the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets for the court gate, and al the pins of the Tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.

39.1: Moreover they made garments of ministration to minister in the Sanctuarie of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet: they made also the holy garments for Aaron, as the Lord had comanded Moses.
39.2: So he made the Ephod of gold, blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen.
39.3: And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into wiers, to work it in ye blew silk and in the purple, and in the skarlet, and in the fine linen, with broydred work.
39.4: For the which they made shoulders to couple together: for it was closed by the two edges thereof.
39.5: And the broydred garde of his Ephod that was upon him, was of the same stuff, and of like work: even of gold, of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
39.6: And they wrought two Onix stones closed in ouches of gold, and graved, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel,
39.7: And put them on the shoulders of the Ephod, as stones for a remembrance of the children of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
39.8: Also he made the brestplate of broydred work like the work of the Ephod: to wit, of gold, blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine twined linen.
39.9: They made the brest plate double, and it was square, an hand breadth long, and an hand breadth broad: it was also double.
39.10: And they filled it with four rowes of stones. The order was thus, a Rubie, a Topaz, and a Carbuncle in the first row:
39.11: And in the second row, an Emeraude, a Saphir, and a Diamond:
39.12: Also in the third row, a Turkeis, an Achate, and an Hematite:
39.13: Likewise in the fourth row, a Chrysolite, an Onix, and a Jasper: closed and set in ouches of gold.
39.14: So the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, even twelve after their names, graven like signets every one after his name according to the twelve tribes.
39.15: After, they made upon the brest plate cheines at the endes, of wrethen work and pure gold.
39.16: They made also two bosses of gold, and two gold rings, and put the two rings in the two corners of the brest plate.
39.17: And they put ye two wrethe cheines of gold in the two rings, in the corners of the brest plate.
39.18: Also the two other endes of the two wrethen chaines they fastened in the two bosses, and put the on the shoulders of the Ephod upon the forefront of it.
39.19: Likewise they made two rings of gold, and put them in the two other corners of the brest plate upon the edge of it, which was on the inside of the Ephod.
39.20: They made also two other golden rings, and put them on the two sides of the Ephod, beneath on the foreside of it, and over against his coupling above the broydered garde of the Ephod.
39.21: Then they fastened the brest plate by his rings unto the rings of the Ephod, with a lace of blew silk, that it might bee fast upon the broydered garde of the Ephod, and that the brest plate should not be loosed from the Ephod, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
39.22: Moreover, he made the robe of the Ephod of woven work, altogether of blew silk.
39.23: And the hole of the robe was in the middes of it, as the coller of an habergeon, with an edge about the coller, that it should not rent.
39.24: And they made upon the skirts of the robe pomegranates, of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, and fine linen twined.
39.25: They made also belles of pure gold and put the belles between the pomegranates upon the skirtes of the robe round about between the pomegranates.
39.26: A bel and a pomegranate, a bel and a pomegranate round about the skirts of the robe to minister in, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
39.27: After, they made coates of fine linen, of woven work for Aaron and for his sonnes.
39.28: And the miter of fine linen, and goodly bonnets of fine linen, and linen breeches of fine twined linen,
39.29: And the girdle of fine twined linen, and of blew silk, and purple, and skarlet, even of needle work, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
39.30: Finally they made the plate for the holy crown of fine gold, and wrote upon it a superscription like to the graving of a signet, HOLINES TO THE LORD.
39.31: And they tied unto it a lace of blew silk to fasten it on hie upon the miter, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
39.32: Thus was all the work of the Tabernacle, even of the Tabernacle of the Congregation finished: and the children of Israel did according to al that the Lord had commanded Moses: so dyd they.
39.33: Afterward they brought the Tabernacle unto Moses, the Tabernacle and al his instruments, his taches, his boards, his barres, and his pillars, and his sockets,
39.34: And the covering of rammes skinnes died red, and the coverings of badgers skinnes, and the covering vail.
39.35: The Ark of the Testimony, and the barres thereof, and the Merciseate,
39.36: The Table, with all the instruments thereof, and the shewebread,
39.37: The pure Candlestick, the lampes thereof, even the lampes set in order, and all the instruments thereof, and the oyle for light:
39.38: Also the golden Altar and the anoynting oyle, and the sweet incense, and the hanging of the Tabernacle door,
39.39: The brasen Altar with his grate of brass, his barres and all his instruments, the Laver and his foot.
39.40: The curtaines of the court with his pillars, and his sockets, and the hanging to the court gate, and his cordes, and his pinnes, and all the instruments of the service of the Tabernacle, called the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
39.41: Finally, the ministring garmentes to serve in the Sanctuarie, and the holy garmentes for Aaron the Priest, and his sonnes garmentes to minister in the Priestes office.
39.42: According to every poynt that the Lord had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
39.43: And Moses beheld al the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded: so had they done: and Moses blessed them.

40.1: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
40.2: In the first day of the first moneth in the very first of the same moneth shalt thou set up the Tabernacle, called ye Tabernacle of the Congregation:
